**[AI/ML Vendor Procurement Playbook]{.underline}**
**Version 3.2 --- March 2025**
**Maintained by: Legal Department & Product Engineering**
**Classification: CONFIDENTIAL --- Internal Use Only**
TechNova Solutions, Inc. 4200 Ridgeline Parkway, Suite 1100 Austin, TX 78735
Right-click to update Table of Contents
**[Section 1 --- Purpose and Scope]{.underline}**

This Playbook governs all procurement of artificial intelligence and machine-learning vendor services by TechNova Solutions, Inc. (\"TechNova\" or the \"Company\"). It establishes the mandatory negotiation positions, acceptable fallback concessions, and walk-away thresholds that must be followed by all personnel involved in the negotiation, drafting, review, and approval of AI/ML vendor agreements on behalf of TechNova.
This Playbook is jointly maintained by two departments within TechNova:
> • **Legal Department**, under the direction of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions (currently Derek Chalmers); and
> • **Product Engineering**, under the direction of the VP of Product Engineering (currently Priya Anand).

These two departments share responsibility for the ongoing development, revision, and dissemination of the Playbook, and all substantive updates require joint sign-off from both maintaining teams prior to publication.

Every AI/ML vendor agreement entered into by TechNova must be negotiated consistent with the positions, fallbacks, and walk-away thresholds set forth herein. No TechNova employee, attorney, or agent is authorized to accept terms that fall below the minimum thresholds established in this Playbook without following the escalation and approval procedures described in Section 2. Compliance with this Playbook is mandatory and will be reviewed as part of the Company\'s internal contract compliance program.

The scope of this Playbook extends to all AI/ML platform agreements, software-as-a-service (SaaS) agreements for AI/ML-enabled tools, model-as-a-service engagements, and any related vendor engagements in which TechNova procures AI or machine-learning capabilities from a third-party vendor. This includes, without limitation, engagements involving large language models, natural language processing platforms, computer vision services, predictive analytics engines, recommendation systems, and any other AI/ML-enabled product or service. The Playbook applies regardless of the TechNova business unit initiating the procurement, and regardless of whether the engagement is structured as a master services agreement, a standalone statement of work, an order form, or any other contractual vehicle.

This is Version 3.2 of the Playbook, effective as of March 2025. Version 3.2 supersedes all prior versions of this Playbook, including Version 3.1 (September 2024), Version 3.0 (March 2024), and all earlier iterations. In the event of any conflict between this Playbook and a prior version, this Playbook controls. A complete version history is set forth in Section 13.
**[Section 2 --- Decision Matrix and Escalation Procedures]{.underline}**
**2.1 --- Classification Framework**

To ensure consistency and clarity in vendor negotiations, this Playbook classifies every material negotiation term according to a three-tier classification framework. Each tier corresponds to a defined level of concession authority and escalation requirement. The three tiers are as follows:

**Green (Preferred Position).** The Green tier represents TechNova\'s standard opening position on each negotiation term. This is the position that should be proposed in every initial draft of a vendor agreement. Acceptance of a Green-tier position by the vendor requires no escalation and no additional approval beyond the negotiating attorney\'s standard authority. The Green position represents TechNova\'s optimal outcome and should be pursued vigorously before any fallback is offered.

**Yellow (Acceptable Fallback).** The Yellow tier represents a concession that falls within an acceptable range below TechNova\'s preferred position. A Yellow-tier concession is one that in-house counsel at the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions level may approve without further escalation. The Yellow tier defines the outer boundary of what TechNova considers a commercially reasonable compromise on a given term. Negotiating attorneys should document the business rationale for accepting a Yellow-tier position in the negotiation file but are not required to seek approval from the VP Legal or General Counsel.

**Red (Walk-Away / Escalation Required).** The Red tier represents a concession that approaches or breaches TechNova\'s minimum acceptable threshold on a given term. A Red-tier position is one that the Company should ordinarily decline. If a negotiating attorney determines that acceptance of a Red-tier position may be warranted by extraordinary business circumstances, that acceptance requires written approval from the VP Legal prior to execution of the agreement. The VP Legal\'s approval must be documented in the deal approval memorandum and must include a written business justification and a description of the risk-mitigation measures that will be implemented.
The following additional rules apply to Red-zone concessions:
> • Any single Red-zone concession on any term in a vendor agreement requires written approval from the VP Legal prior to execution.

> • Two or more simultaneous Red-zone concessions on any single vendor agreement require joint approval from the VP Legal and the General Counsel. In such cases, the deal approval memorandum must include an enhanced risk assessment and a written recommendation from the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions.
**2.2 --- Summary Decision Matrix**

The following table provides a summary-level decision matrix for each major term category addressed in this Playbook. Detailed negotiation guidance, including specific thresholds, examples, and fallback positions, is set forth in the referenced sections.

**Term Category**                    **Green (Preferred)**                                                                                          **Yellow (Acceptable)**                                                                        **Red (Walk-Away)**                                                                                                   **Section Reference**

IP Ownership & Licensing             Full ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations                                                                 Irrevocable perpetual license with portability, escrow, and non-assertion                      Less than perpetual license with 30-day extraction rights                                                             Section 3

Data Processing & Privacy            Full DPA with service-provider designation, third-party training prohibition, and verified de-identification   Mandatory requirements are non-negotiable (no Yellow tier)                                     Any deviation from mandatory requirements                                                                             Section 4

Liability Framework                  General cap at 2× annual fees; uncapped IP indemnity and data breach                                           General cap at 1.5× annual fees; super-cap ≥ 3× annual fees for IP indemnity and data breach   General cap below 1× annual fees; super-cap below 3× annual fees; any cap on willful misconduct or gross negligence   Section 5

Service Level Agreements             99.95%+ uptime; p95 ≤ 400 ms; F1 ≥ 0.95; credits ≥ 30% monthly fees                                            99.95% uptime; p95 ≤ 500 ms; F1 ≥ 0.92; credits ≥ 20% monthly fees                             Below 99.95% uptime; p95 \> 500 ms; F1 \< 0.92; credits \< 20% monthly fees                                           Section 6

Source Code / Model Escrow           Iron Mountain IPM; full deposit scope                                                                          Tier 1 alternative; full deposit scope                                                         No escrow for TCV \> \$1M                                                                                             Section 7

Insurance Requirements               Tech E&O at \$10M (TCV \> \$5M)                                                                                Tech E&O at \$5M                                                                               Tech E&O below \$5M                                                                                                   Section 8

AI-Output Risk Allocation            Full vendor indemnity for output-related claims                                                                Shared-risk framework with vendor first-dollar coverage                                        No coverage for output-related claims                                                                                 Section 9

Governing Law & Dispute Resolution   Delaware law; Delaware courts                                                                                  New York or Texas law; NY or TX courts                                                         Other jurisdictions; mandatory arbitration for disputes \> \$1M                                                       Section 10

Indemnification                      All IP rights; authorized use coverage                                                                         Non-negotiable (no Yellow tier for scope)                                                      Limited to registered U.S. patents/copyrights                                                                         Section 11
**2.3 --- Escalation Procedures**
The escalation path for all AI/ML vendor negotiations follows the chain of authority set forth below:
1\. **Negotiating Attorney** --- responsible for conducting the negotiation consistent with this Playbook, identifying the tier classification of each material term, and escalating as required.

2\. **Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions** (currently Derek Chalmers) --- has authority to approve Yellow-zone concessions without further escalation. Serves as the first level of escalation for questions of interpretation under this Playbook.
3\. **VP Legal** --- required approval authority for any single Red-zone concession. Serves as the second level of escalation.

4\. **General Counsel** --- required co-approval authority (together with the VP Legal) for two or more simultaneous Red-zone concessions on any single vendor agreement. Serves as the final level of escalation.

Any acceptance of a Red-zone term must be documented in the deal approval memorandum. The memorandum must include, at minimum: (a) a description of the Red-zone concession and the vendor\'s stated rationale for its position; (b) a business justification for TechNova\'s acceptance of the concession; (c) a description of the risk-mitigation measures that will be implemented to address the risk associated with the concession; and (d) the written approval of the VP Legal (and, if applicable, the General Counsel).

Outside counsel may be engaged at the discretion of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions for any AI/ML vendor engagement. Engagement of outside counsel is particularly recommended in the following circumstances:
> • Any engagement with a total contract value (\"TCV\") exceeding \$5,000,000.

> • Any engagement involving novel or untested AI/ML risk allocation issues, including but not limited to novel AI-output indemnity structures, regulatory compliance frameworks for generative AI, or cross-border data processing arrangements.
> • Any engagement where the vendor\'s proposed terms deviate materially from the positions established in this Playbook and the appropriate response is unclear.

TechNova\'s preferred outside counsel for AI/ML vendor transactions is Kirkstead & Yao LLP. Engagement of Kirkstead & Yao LLP or any other outside counsel must be authorized in writing by the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions and must comply with TechNova\'s outside counsel engagement policies.
**[Section 3 --- IP Ownership & Licensing]{.underline}**
**3.1 --- Preferred Position (Green)**
TechNova\'s standard opening position on intellectual property ownership and licensing is as follows:

**Ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations.** TechNova owns all model artifacts that are derived from or trained on TechNova\'s data, including but not limited to: fine-tuned weights, adapter layers (including LoRA and QLoRA adapters), embeddings, vector representations, and any derivative models that incorporate TechNova data in any form (collectively, \"Customer-Trained Adaptations\"). This ownership extends to all rights, title, and interest in and to the Customer-Trained Adaptations, including all intellectual property rights therein, and such ownership vests automatically upon creation without the need for any further action or assignment.

**Vendor Retention of Base Model IP.** The vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing base model (the \"Base Model\") and all platform intellectual property that existed prior to the engagement or that is developed by the vendor independently of TechNova\'s data and without use of TechNova\'s confidential information. For the avoidance of doubt, the vendor\'s retained ownership does not extend to any Customer-Trained Adaptations, regardless of whether such adaptations are implemented on or integrated with the vendor\'s Base Model.

**License to Base Model.** TechNova receives an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, fully sublicensable license to the vendor\'s Base Model solely as necessary to operate, deploy, maintain, and update the Customer-Trained Adaptations. This license survives expiration or termination of the agreement for any reason and includes the right to use the Base Model in production environments, disaster recovery environments, and development and testing environments as reasonably necessary for the operation of the Customer-Trained Adaptations.
This Green-tier position should be included in every initial draft of an AI/ML vendor agreement. It requires no escalation and no additional approval.
**3.2 --- Acceptable Fallback (Yellow)**

Where a vendor will not agree to assign ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations to TechNova, TechNova will accept, as an alternative, an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to all fine-tuned adapter weights and related Customer-Trained Adaptations, provided that all of the following conditions are met:

**Portability.** The vendor must provide an API-based or otherwise automated export of all Customer-Trained Adaptations in an industry-standard format (e.g., ONNX, SafeTensors, or other format mutually agreed upon at contract execution) within thirty (30) days of the termination or expiration of the agreement. The export must include all artifacts necessary for TechNova to deploy the Customer-Trained Adaptations on an alternative platform without material degradation in performance. The vendor may not condition the export on the payment of additional fees beyond those already payable under the agreement.

**Escrow.** All Customer-Trained Adaptations, together with training configuration files (including hyperparameters and training scripts) and pipeline artifacts necessary to reproduce or redeploy the fine-tuned model, must be deposited in escrow in accordance with the requirements set forth in Section 7 of this Playbook. The escrow deposit must be updated at least quarterly and upon any material model version update.

**Non-Assertion.** The vendor grants TechNova a perpetual, irrevocable covenant not to assert any intellectual property rights --- including patent, copyright, trade secret, and any other IP rights --- against TechNova\'s use, deployment, modification, or further development of Customer-Trained Adaptations, including post-termination use. This non-assertion covenant runs with any successor, assignee, or acquirer of the vendor\'s intellectual property rights.

This fallback position falls within the Yellow zone and may be approved by the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions without further escalation, provided that all three conditions (portability, escrow, and non-assertion) are satisfied in full.
**3.3 --- Minimum Requirement / Walk-Away Threshold (Red)**

At absolute minimum, the agreement must grant TechNova a perpetual license to the Customer-Trained Adaptations that survives the termination or expiration of the agreement for any reason, together with extraction rights permitting TechNova to export all Customer-Trained Adaptations within thirty (30) days of termination or expiration.

Any vendor position that does not include at least a perpetual, surviving license with thirty-day extraction rights constitutes a walk-away and must not be accepted without written approval from the VP Legal. The VP Legal\'s approval must include a documented business justification explaining why the engagement is sufficiently critical to justify acceptance of a below-threshold IP position, together with a description of the alternative risk-mitigation measures (e.g., enhanced escrow, accelerated transition support) that will be implemented.
The following specific vendor positions fall within the Red zone:
> • A vendor position granting only a term-limited license that expires upon termination of the agreement, with no surviving rights to the Customer-Trained Adaptations.

> • A vendor position that conditions post-termination use of Customer-Trained Adaptations on the payment of additional license fees, maintenance fees, or any other fees not included in the original agreement pricing.
> • A vendor position that grants TechNova a surviving license but does not include extraction rights, or that conditions extraction on a timeframe longer than thirty (30) days.
**3.4 --- Negotiation Guidance**
Negotiating attorneys should adhere to the following approach when negotiating IP ownership and licensing terms with AI/ML vendors:

Open every negotiation with the full ownership position set forth in Section 3.1. Present TechNova\'s rationale clearly: the Customer-Trained Adaptations are derived from TechNova\'s proprietary data, and TechNova\'s investment in data curation, annotation, and preparation justifies ownership of the resulting artifacts. Many vendors will be receptive to this position, particularly where TechNova\'s data is the primary driver of the fine-tuning process.

If the vendor resists full ownership, move to the irrevocable perpetual license with portability, escrow, and non-assertion conditions set forth in Section 3.2. This concession does not require escalation and should be presented as a commercially reasonable compromise that protects both parties\' interests. Emphasize to the vendor that the non-assertion covenant and escrow requirements are essential counterbalances to TechNova\'s concession on ownership.

Under no circumstances should the negotiating attorney concede the thirty-day extraction window. The thirty-day period is a hard floor across all tiers of the classification framework. If a vendor proposes a longer extraction window (e.g., 60 or 90 days), this is not within the Yellow zone and must be treated as a Red-zone concession.

Finally, all IP ownership and licensing provisions must be reviewed for consistency with the escrow requirements in Section 7 and the indemnification scope in Section 11. The negotiating attorney should ensure that the escrow deposit scope in the agreement matches the defined scope of \"Customer-Trained Adaptations,\" and that the vendor\'s IP indemnification obligation extends to TechNova\'s authorized use of Customer-Trained Adaptations in addition to the vendor\'s Base Model and platform.
**[Section 4 --- Data Processing & Privacy]{.underline}**
**4.1 --- Regulatory Framework**

TechNova processes consumer nonpublic personal information (\"NPPI\") as part of its financial technology product offerings, including its LendStream platform and related consumer-facing services. As a result, TechNova is subject to, and must ensure vendor compliance with, the following key regulatory frameworks:

**Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (\"GLBA\").** TechNova is a financial institution within the meaning of the GLBA and its implementing regulations, including the FTC\'s Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314). Any AI/ML vendor that receives, processes, stores, or otherwise has access to NPPI in connection with the provision of services to TechNova must comply with the GLBA\'s privacy and safeguarding requirements, including the obligation to maintain an information security program that meets the standards prescribed by the Safeguards Rule.

**California Consumer Privacy Act / California Privacy Rights Act (\"CCPA/CPRA\").** TechNova processes the personal information of California residents and is subject to the CCPA, as amended by the CPRA, and the regulations promulgated thereunder by the California Privacy Protection Agency (\"CPPA\"). All AI/ML vendor agreements involving access to personal information of California residents must comply with the CCPA/CPRA\'s requirements for service-provider relationships, including the contractual certifications and restrictions described in Section 4.2 below.

All AI/ML vendor agreements involving access to TechNova customer data --- whether such access is direct (e.g., the vendor receives raw customer data for model training) or indirect (e.g., the vendor\'s platform processes customer data in real time during inference) --- must comply with both the GLBA and the CCPA/CPRA. Compliance with these regulatory frameworks is a threshold requirement for any AI/ML vendor engagement and is not subject to trade-offs or concessions in other areas of the negotiation.
**4.2 --- Mandatory Requirements (All Zones --- Non-Negotiable)**

The following requirements apply to every AI/ML vendor agreement involving access to TechNova customer data. These requirements are mandatory and non-negotiable. They apply regardless of whether the vendor\'s position on a given term falls within the Green, Yellow, or Red zone for other provisions. No concession on any other term in the agreement may be offered or accepted in exchange for a relaxation of these requirements.

**Service-Provider / Processor Designation.** The vendor must contractually agree to act as a \"service provider\" as defined in California Civil Code Section 1798.140(ag) with respect to all personal information of California residents that the vendor receives, processes, or accesses in connection with the agreement. Where applicable, the vendor must also agree to act as a \"processor\" under the GLBA and its implementing regulations, and to comply with all obligations imposed on processors under those regulations. This designation is mandatory and non-negotiable. A vendor that refuses to accept a service-provider designation, or that insists on being treated as an independent \"business\" or \"controller\" with respect to TechNova customer data, presents a fundamental compliance risk that cannot be mitigated through other contractual mechanisms.

**Data Processing Agreement (DPA).** Every AI/ML vendor agreement must include a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) as an exhibit, schedule, or appendix to the agreement, or as a standalone agreement executed concurrently with the vendor agreement. The DPA must contain, at minimum, the following provisions:

> \(a\) **CCPA Service-Provider Certification.** A certification by the vendor that it understands and will comply with the restrictions applicable to service providers under the CCPA, including the restrictions set forth in California Civil Code Section 1798.140(ag), and that it will not retain, use, or disclose personal information received from TechNova for any purpose other than the specific business purpose set forth in the DPA.

> \(b\) **Specification of Business Purpose.** A clear and specific description of the business purpose(s) for which the vendor is authorized to process TechNova customer data. The business purpose must be defined with sufficient specificity to enable TechNova to verify compliance and must not include broad or open-ended language (e.g., \"improving vendor\'s products and services\" is not an acceptable business purpose).

> \(c\) **Prohibition on Sale or Sharing.** An express prohibition on the vendor\'s sale or sharing (as those terms are defined in the CCPA/CPRA) of TechNova customer data, including any personal information derived from or based on TechNova customer data.

> \(d\) **72-Hour Data Breach Notification.** An obligation on the vendor to notify TechNova in writing within seventy-two (72) hours of the vendor\'s discovery of any actual or reasonably suspected data breach, security incident, or unauthorized access, acquisition, use, or disclosure of TechNova customer data. The notification must include, to the extent known, the nature of the incident, the categories and approximate number of records affected, the vendor\'s assessment of the likely impact, and the remediation measures being implemented.

> \(e\) **Sub-Processor Engagement Restrictions.** A requirement that the vendor may not engage any sub-processor to process TechNova customer data without TechNova\'s prior written consent. The vendor must provide TechNova with a current list of sub-processors at the time of contract execution and must notify TechNova in writing at least thirty (30) days prior to any proposed addition or replacement of a sub-processor.

**Prohibition on Third-Party Model Training.** The vendor must be contractually prohibited from using TechNova customer data --- including any derivatives, transformations, embeddings, or representations thereof --- for training, improving, fine-tuning, or otherwise enhancing any models or algorithms for the benefit of third parties or for the benefit of the vendor\'s general-purpose product offerings. This prohibition must extend to all forms of the data, including de-identified or aggregated forms, unless a specific de-identification right has been negotiated in accordance with Section 4.3 below. This prohibition is absolute and non-negotiable.
**4.3 --- De-Identification Standards**

In certain engagements, a vendor may seek the right to use de-identified or aggregated data derived from TechNova customer data for the purpose of improving the vendor\'s models, algorithms, or platform capabilities. TechNova may consider granting such a right, but only under the following conditions:

**Statutory Standard.** The de-identification must meet the statutory standard set forth in the CCPA at California Civil Code Section 1798.140(m). Specifically, the information must be information that cannot reasonably be used to infer information about, or otherwise be linked to, a particular consumer or household, provided that the vendor (a) has implemented technical safeguards and business processes that prohibit re-identification of the consumer to whom the information may pertain; (b) has implemented business processes to prevent inadvertent release of de-identified information; and (c) makes no attempt to re-identify the information.

**Independent Third-Party Verification.** The de-identification process and its compliance with the statutory standard must be verified by an independent third-party auditor. The auditor must be approved by TechNova in writing prior to the commencement of any audit. The auditor must provide a written certification that the de-identification meets the statutory standard, and this certification must be provided to TechNova before the vendor may make any use of the de-identified data.

**Classification.** Any de-identification right is within the Yellow zone only if both conditions above (statutory standard compliance and independent verification) are satisfied in full. If the vendor proposes a de-identification right without independent third-party verification, or if the proposed de-identification standard does not meet the CCPA statutory standard, the concession falls within the Red zone and requires VP Legal approval before acceptance.
**4.4 --- Negotiation Guidance**

The service-provider designation and the DPA with CCPA certification are foundational compliance requirements. These terms must appear in every AI/ML vendor agreement and must not be traded for concessions in other areas of the negotiation --- not for more favorable pricing, not for enhanced SLAs, and not for any other commercial benefit.

If a vendor proposes a \"controller-to-controller\" or \"independent contractor\" data relationship --- in which the vendor would process TechNova customer data as an independent business or controller with its own rights to use the data --- this is a walk-away absent extraordinary circumstances approved by the General Counsel. A controller-to-controller relationship would expose TechNova to significant regulatory risk under both the GLBA and the CCPA/CPRA, including potential liability for the vendor\'s independent use of customer data, and would undermine TechNova\'s ability to comply with its own privacy obligations to its customers.

Negotiating attorneys should be alert to vendor drafting that attempts to achieve a de facto controller relationship through indirect means, such as broadly defined business purposes, retained rights to \"aggregate\" or \"anonymized\" data without adequate de-identification standards, or carve-outs from the service-provider restrictions for \"product improvement\" or \"model training.\" Any such drafting should be redlined and replaced with the mandatory provisions described in Section 4.2.
**[Section 5 --- Liability Framework]{.underline}**
**5.1 --- General Liability Cap**

The general limitation of liability in any AI/ML vendor agreement sets the maximum aggregate amount that the vendor may be required to pay to TechNova (and vice versa) for all claims arising under the agreement, subject to the carve-outs described in Section 5.2. The following thresholds apply:

**Green (Preferred).** TechNova\'s preferred position is a general liability cap set at two times (2×) the annual fees payable under the agreement. For example, for an agreement with annual fees of \$2,400,000, the preferred general liability cap would be \$4,800,000. This position should be proposed in every initial draft.

**Yellow (Acceptable).** If the vendor will not agree to a 2× annual fees cap, TechNova will accept a general liability cap at one and one-half times (1.5×) the annual fees payable under the agreement. For an agreement with annual fees of \$2,400,000, the acceptable general liability cap would be \$3,600,000. This concession falls within the Yellow zone and may be approved by the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions without further escalation.

**Red (Walk-Away).** Any general liability cap that falls below one times (1×) the annual fees payable under the agreement is a walk-away. For an agreement with annual fees of \$2,400,000, the walk-away floor is \$2,400,000. Acceptance of a general liability cap at or below 1× annual fees requires written approval from the VP Legal, with documented business justification and risk-mitigation measures.

For the avoidance of doubt, the annual fees used to calculate the liability cap should be the annual fees payable in the first year of the agreement (or, for multi-year agreements with escalating fees, the average annual fees over the initial term), unless a different calculation methodology is negotiated. Negotiating attorneys should ensure that the cap is calculated on a consistent basis and that the calculation methodology is clearly stated in the agreement.
**5.2 --- Uncapped Carve-Outs**

Certain categories of liability must be carved out from the general liability cap to ensure that TechNova has adequate recourse in the event of the vendor\'s most serious breaches. The following framework applies:

**Mandatory (Non-Negotiable).** The following categories of liability must remain uncapped --- that is, excluded entirely from the general liability cap --- regardless of the general cap amount negotiated. These carve-outs are mandatory and non-negotiable:
> • **Willful misconduct.** Any liability arising from the vendor\'s willful misconduct.
> • **Gross negligence.** Any liability arising from the vendor\'s gross negligence.

Any vendor attempt to impose a cap on liability for willful misconduct or gross negligence is a Red-zone position and a walk-away. There are no circumstances under which TechNova should accept a cap on these categories.
**Green (Preferred).** In addition to the mandatory carve-outs for willful misconduct and gross negligence, TechNova\'s preferred position is that the following categories also remain fully uncapped:
> • **IP indemnification obligations.** The vendor\'s indemnification obligations with respect to intellectual property infringement claims, as described in Section 11.

> • **Data breach and data privacy obligations.** The vendor\'s liability for breaches of its data processing and privacy obligations, as described in Section 4, including liability arising from unauthorized access to, disclosure of, or loss of TechNova customer data.

**Yellow (Acceptable).** If the vendor will not agree to fully uncapped IP indemnification and data breach obligations, TechNova will accept a \"super-cap\" --- that is, an elevated liability cap for these specific categories --- at a minimum of three times (3×) the annual fees payable under the agreement. For an agreement with annual fees of \$2,400,000, the minimum acceptable super-cap is \$7,200,000. This super-cap applies only to the IP indemnification and data breach carve-outs; the mandatory carve-outs for willful misconduct and gross negligence remain fully uncapped regardless.
**Red (Walk-Away).** Any of the following positions is a walk-away:
> • A super-cap for IP indemnification and data breach obligations that falls below 3× the annual fees.
> • Any attempt by the vendor to cap liability for willful misconduct or gross negligence, whether through the general cap, a super-cap, or any other mechanism.
**5.3 --- Negotiation Guidance**
Negotiating attorneys should approach liability framework discussions using the following strategy:

Open at 2× annual fees for the general cap and propose fully uncapped treatment for IP indemnity and data breach obligations, in addition to the mandatory uncapped treatment of willful misconduct and gross negligence. This is the Green-tier position and represents TechNova\'s optimal outcome.

If the vendor resists, the following represents an acceptable compromise landing zone: a general cap of 1.5× annual fees, with a super-cap of 3× annual fees for IP indemnity and data breach carve-outs, plus fully uncapped liability for willful misconduct and gross negligence. This combination falls within the Yellow zone and does not require escalation beyond the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions.

Be alert to vendor proposals that use trailing-fee-based caps rather than annual-fee-based caps. Some vendors will propose caps based on the fees paid or payable during the preceding six-month or twelve-month period (e.g., \"not to exceed the fees paid by Customer in the six months preceding the claim\"). If the vendor proposes a trailing-fee-based cap, convert the proposed cap to its annual-fee equivalent and evaluate it against the thresholds set forth above. A cap based on six months of trailing fees, for example, is equivalent to approximately 0.5× annual fees and would fall below the Red-zone floor.

All liability positions --- including the general cap, the super-cap (if applicable), and the carve-out structure --- must be documented in the deal approval memorandum for every AI/ML vendor agreement.
**[Section 6 --- Service Level Agreements (SLAs)]{.underline}**
**6.1 --- Uptime / Availability**

**Minimum (Non-Negotiable).** The vendor must commit to a monthly uptime percentage of at least 99.95%, measured across all production endpoints made available to TechNova under the agreement. This equates to a maximum permissible downtime of approximately 21 minutes and 54 seconds per month. This threshold is non-negotiable and applies to all AI/ML vendor engagements regardless of the business unit, use case, or TCV.

Scheduled maintenance windows may be excluded from the uptime calculation, provided that (a) the vendor provides TechNova with at least seventy-two (72) hours\' advance written notice of each scheduled maintenance window; (b) scheduled maintenance is limited to off-peak hours as mutually agreed by the parties; and (c) scheduled maintenance windows do not, in aggregate, exceed four (4) hours per calendar month. Force majeure events may also be excluded from the uptime calculation, provided that the force majeure provision is narrowly defined and limited to events that are genuinely beyond the vendor\'s reasonable control (e.g., natural disasters, government actions, widespread internet outages), and does not include events that are within the vendor\'s control or that a reasonably prudent vendor could have anticipated or mitigated (e.g., vendor infrastructure failures, capacity shortfalls, software bugs).
**6.2 --- Latency**

**Green (Preferred).** TechNova\'s preferred latency commitment is a p95 response latency of no more than four hundred milliseconds (≤ 400 ms), measured at the vendor\'s API gateway for production inference requests. This threshold is required for real-time, customer-facing applications, including the LendStream product line and any other deployment that involves real-time decisioning, scoring, or response generation in interaction with end users.

**Yellow (Acceptable).** If the vendor cannot commit to ≤ 400 ms p95 latency, TechNova will accept a p95 response latency of no more than five hundred milliseconds (≤ 500 ms). A vendor offer in the range of 401--500 ms falls within the acceptable zone but below the preferred threshold. Negotiating attorneys should make a good-faith effort to secure a commitment at or below 400 ms before accepting a latency commitment in the 401--500 ms range.

If the vendor\'s best offer falls within the 401--500 ms range (e.g., 450 ms p95), the negotiating attorney should flag the offer to Product Engineering for confirmation that the specific use case can tolerate the additional latency. For example, a 450 ms commitment may be acceptable for batch processing or non-time-critical analytics, but may not be acceptable for LendStream real-time decisioning, where even 50 ms of additional latency can materially affect conversion rates and customer experience. Product Engineering confirmation should be documented in the negotiation file before the concession is accepted.

**Red (Walk-Away).** Any latency commitment above 500 ms p95 is a walk-away for customer-facing AI deployments. This threshold applies to any deployment that directly serves or interacts with TechNova\'s customers in real time. For internal-only, non-customer-facing deployments (e.g., internal analytics, back-office model inference), the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions may approve a latency commitment above 500 ms on a case-by-case basis, subject to Product Engineering\'s written confirmation that the higher latency does not impact customer experience.
**6.3 --- Model Accuracy**

**Green (Preferred).** TechNova\'s preferred model accuracy commitment is an F1 score of at least 0.95 on agreed benchmark datasets. The benchmark datasets must be mutually agreed upon at the time of contract execution and must be representative of TechNova\'s production data distribution. The F1 score should be calculated on the basis of the agreed evaluation methodology, including the specific precision and recall definitions applicable to TechNova\'s use case.

**Yellow (Acceptable).** TechNova will accept a model accuracy commitment with an F1 score of at least 0.92 on agreed benchmark datasets. An F1 score of 0.92 is the Playbook minimum; no accuracy commitment below this threshold is acceptable without escalation.

**Red (Walk-Away).** Any accuracy commitment below an F1 score of 0.92 is a walk-away. A vendor that cannot commit to at least F1 ≥ 0.92 on agreed benchmark datasets is not able to meet TechNova\'s minimum performance requirements.

Where a vendor proposes a post-deployment ramp period (e.g., a 90-day stabilization period during which the model is tuned to TechNova\'s production data), the following approach is acceptable: the ramp target may begin at the Yellow floor (F1 ≥ 0.92) at the commencement of the stabilization period, provided that the agreement requires the vendor to achieve the preferred threshold (F1 ≥ 0.95, or such other post-stabilization target as may be negotiated) by the end of the stabilization period. If the vendor fails to achieve the post-stabilization target by the end of the ramp period, TechNova must have the right to terminate the agreement without penalty.
**6.4 --- Service Credits**

**Green (Preferred).** TechNova\'s preferred position on service credits is that credits should be calculated as a meaningful percentage of the monthly fees payable under the agreement, with a credit cap of at least thirty percent (30%) of monthly fees per month. The credit schedule should provide graduated credits tied to the severity of the SLA breach (e.g., 10% credit for uptime between 99.90% and 99.95%; 20% credit for uptime between 99.50% and 99.89%; 30% credit for uptime below 99.50%).

**Yellow (Acceptable / Floor).** The minimum acceptable credit cap is twenty percent (20%) of monthly fees per month. For an agreement with monthly fees of \$200,000, the minimum acceptable monthly credit cap is \$40,000. This is a hard floor.
**Red (Walk-Away).** Any credit cap below twenty percent (20%) of monthly fees is a walk-away and requires VP Legal approval before acceptance.

Credits must be automatic --- that is, applied to TechNova\'s account without requiring TechNova to file a claim, submit a ticket, or take any affirmative action --- or, at minimum, triggered by a simple written notice from TechNova (e.g., an email to a designated vendor contact) without the need for detailed documentation or formal dispute procedures. Any credit mechanism that requires TechNova to submit detailed incident reports, wait for vendor investigation, or participate in a multi-step claims process before credits are applied is not acceptable and should be redlined.
**6.5 --- Chronic Underperformance and Termination Right**

Every AI/ML vendor agreement must include a termination right that may be exercised by TechNova in the event of chronic SLA underperformance. Chronic underperformance is defined as a material SLA miss --- including uptime, latency, or accuracy failures --- in three (3) or more consecutive calendar months.

If TechNova exercises its termination right for chronic underperformance, the termination must be effective without the imposition of any termination fees, early-termination penalties, or other charges beyond the fees already accrued for services rendered through the effective date of termination. The vendor must also provide reasonable transition assistance (at no additional cost) for a period of at least ninety (90) days following the effective date of termination.
**6.6 --- Negotiation Guidance**

Uptime at 99.95% is a hard floor and must not be negotiated below this level under any circumstances. If a vendor proposes a lower uptime commitment (e.g., 99.9% or 99.5%), this is a Red-zone position and a walk-away.

For latency, the negotiating attorney should push firmly for a commitment at or below 400 ms p95, especially for any deployment supporting the LendStream platform or other real-time consumer-facing products. If the vendor counters with a latency commitment between 400 ms and 500 ms, the negotiating attorney should coordinate with the VP of Product Engineering (currently Priya Anand) before accepting. Product Engineering\'s assessment of whether the specific use case can tolerate the proposed latency should be documented in the negotiation file.

For accuracy, an F1 score of 0.92 is the absolute minimum; the preferred threshold is 0.95. A stabilization ramp period is acceptable only if the post-stabilization target meets or exceeds the preferred threshold, and only if the agreement provides TechNova with a termination right if the target is not achieved by the end of the ramp period.
Credit caps below 20% of monthly fees are Red zone. Do not accept a credit cap below this floor without VP Legal approval and a documented business justification.
**[Section 7 --- Source Code / Model Escrow]{.underline}**
**7.1 --- Escrow Threshold**

Escrow is mandatory for any AI/ML vendor engagement with a total contract value (\"TCV\") exceeding one million dollars (\$1,000,000). The TCV calculation includes all fees payable under the agreement over the initial term, including platform fees, implementation fees, usage-based fees (estimated at projected usage), and any other fees or charges payable to the vendor.

There is no exception to this requirement. If the TCV exceeds \$1,000,000, the escrow provision must be included in the agreement itself (as a section or exhibit) or in a standalone three-party escrow agreement executed concurrently with the vendor agreement. An AI/ML vendor agreement with a TCV exceeding \$1,000,000 that does not include an escrow provision --- or that is not accompanied by a concurrently executed standalone escrow agreement --- may not be approved for execution.
**7.2 --- Deposit Scope**
The escrow deposit must include, at minimum, the following materials:

> \(a\) **Fine-Tuned Model Weights.** All fine-tuned model weights, including adapter weights (e.g., LoRA adapters), embeddings, and any other model parameters specific to TechNova\'s deployment. The deposited weights must correspond to the production version of the model currently deployed for TechNova.

> \(b\) **Training Configuration Files.** All training configuration files, including hyperparameter configurations, training scripts, data preprocessing pipelines, feature engineering code, and any other files or scripts necessary to understand and reproduce the training process that produced the fine-tuned model.

> \(c\) **Pipeline Artifacts.** All pipeline artifacts necessary to reproduce or redeploy the fine-tuned model in a production environment, including inference code, model serving configurations, dependency specifications (e.g., requirements.txt, Dockerfile), and documentation describing the deployment architecture and environment requirements.

Deposits must be updated no less frequently than quarterly (i.e., at least once every ninety (90) calendar days), or upon any material model version update (e.g., retraining, architecture change, or significant hyperparameter adjustment), whichever is more frequent. Each deposit update must be accompanied by a verification report from the escrow agent confirming receipt and completeness of the deposit materials.
**7.3 --- Preferred Escrow Agent**

**Preferred.** TechNova\'s preferred escrow agent is Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. (\"Iron Mountain IPM\"). Iron Mountain IPM has demonstrated experience in technology escrow generally and has developed specific capabilities and processes for AI/ML model artifact escrow, including secure handling of large binary model files, support for quarterly deposit updates, and familiarity with the unique verification challenges associated with neural network weight files and training artifacts.

**Acceptable Alternative.** If the vendor has a pre-existing relationship with an alternative escrow agent, TechNova will accept any Tier 1 technology escrow provider with demonstrated experience in AI/ML model artifact escrow. Currently, the following providers are recognized as acceptable Tier 1 alternatives:
> • NCC Group plc
> • Other providers with demonstrated AI/ML model artifact escrow capabilities, subject to case-by-case approval by the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions.

A complete list of approved and acceptable escrow agents is maintained in Appendix B. Escrow agent selection should be proposed by TechNova in the initial draft of the agreement. If the vendor proposes an alternative agent, the negotiating attorney should evaluate the proposed agent against the selection criteria set forth in Appendix B and consult with the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions if the proposed agent is not already on the approved list.
**7.4 --- Release Triggers**
The escrow materials must be released to TechNova upon the occurrence of any of the following trigger events:

> \(a\) **Insolvency.** The vendor files a voluntary petition for bankruptcy, has an involuntary petition for bankruptcy filed against it that is not dismissed within sixty (60) days, makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or becomes the subject of any similar insolvency proceeding.

> \(b\) **Uncured Material Breach.** The vendor commits a material breach of the agreement that remains uncured for more than sixty (60) days following TechNova\'s delivery of written notice of the breach to the vendor and to the escrow agent. The notice must identify the breach with reasonable specificity and state TechNova\'s intent to invoke the escrow release upon expiration of the cure period.

Vendor shall perform the following Implementation Services in connection with the deployment and configuration of the Platform for Customer\'s use with LendStream:

> \(c\) The total duration of scheduled maintenance does not exceed four (4) hours in any single calendar month.

Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours\' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
**3. Force Majeure Exclusion**
Downtime resulting from Force Majeure Events, as defined in Section 14.5 of the Agreement, shall be excluded from the calculation of Platform availability for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
**4. Service Credit Schedule --- Uptime Failures**

In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA in any calendar month, Customer shall be entitled to a Service Credit calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment (\$200,000) for the affected calendar month, in accordance with the following tiered schedule:
**Monthly Uptime Achieved**         **Service Credit (% of Monthly Fee)**
\[ADDED: \### 4A. Service Credit Schedule --- Latency Failures

If p95 latency exceeds 400 ms for any calendar month, an additional Service Credit of 5% of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment (\$10,000) shall apply, subject to the overall monthly cap set forth in Section 5(c).\]
\[ADDED: \### 4B. Service Credit Schedule --- Accuracy Failures

If the F1 score falls below 0.94 for two (2) consecutive quarterly measurements (post-Stabilization Period), an additional Service Credit of 10% of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment (\$20,000) shall apply, subject to the overall monthly cap set forth in Section 5(c).\]
**5. Service Credit Terms and Conditions**

> \(a\) **Request Requirement.** To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor\'s support team within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the SLA failure occurred. The request must identify the specific dates and times of the SLA failure and reference the applicable monthly service report. Vendor shall validate the claim against its monitoring data and notify Customer of the approved Service Credit amount within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of the request.

> \(b\) **Application of Credits.** Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against the next invoice(s) issued to Customer under the Agreement. If this Agreement is terminated or expires and a balance of unapplied Service Credits remains, Vendor shall refund such balance in cash within thirty (30) days.

> \(c\) **Maximum Credits.** In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed thirty percent (30%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month (i.e., \$ 60,000). Service Credits are cumulative across SLA categories (Uptime, Latency, and Accuracy) but shall not exceed the thirty percent (30%) monthly cap in aggregate. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year.

> \(d\) \*\* Remedies.\*\* Service Credits are not Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures. Customer retains all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, including the termination right under Section 9.5 of the Agreement.
**6. \[DELETED: Latency and Accuracy\] \[ADDED: Termination Trigger\]**

If Vendor fails to meet any SLA target (Uptime, Latency, or Accuracy) for three (3) or more consecutive calendar months, Customer may terminate the Agreement upon thirty (30) days\' written notice in accordance with Section 9.5 of the Agreement, without payment of any early termination fee.

(\"**Customer**\"). This Acceptable Use Policy supplements the use restrictions set forth in Section 2.3 of the Agreement.
**1. Authorized Use**

Customer shall use the Platform solely for the processing, analysis, and classification of Customer Data in connection with Customer\'s LendStream product, as authorized under Section 2.2 of the Agreement.
**2. Prohibited Use**
Customer shall not use the Platform to process data of third parties other than Customer\'s end-user consumers in connection with LendStream.

**DATA PROCESSING ADDENDUM**

This Data Processing Addendum (\"**DPA**\") is attached to and forms part of the AI Platform Agreement dated as of April 2, 2025 (the \"**Agreement**\"), between Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC (\"**Vendor**\") and TechNova Solutions, Inc. (\"**Customer**\"). This DPA is entered into pursuant to Section 6.8 of the Agreement. In the event of any conflict between this DPA and the Agreement, this DPA shall control with respect to data protection matters.
**1. Scope.** This DPA applies to Vendor\'s processing of Customer Data as a service provider/processor on behalf of Customer.
**2. Role of the Parties**
Customer is the controller/business with respect to Customer Data. Vendor is the processor/service provider with respect to Customer Data and shall process Customer Data solely on behalf of Customer.
**3. CCPA/CPRA Service-Provider Certification**

Vendor certifies that it is a \"service provider\" as defined in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag), and that it shall not sell, share, or retain Customer Data except as necessary to perform its obligations under the Agreement.
**4. GLBA Compliance**
Vendor acknowledges that Customer Data includes consumer NPPI subject to the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act and agrees to comply with all applicable safeguard requirements thereunder.
**5. Processing Instructions**
Vendor shall process Customer Data solely in accordance with Customer\'s documented instructions as set forth in the Agreement.
**6. Sub-Processor Requirements**

Vendor shall not engage any sub-processor to process Customer Data without Customer\'s prior written consent. Vendor shall impose data protection obligations on sub-processors that are no less protective than those set forth in this DPA and the Agreement. Vendor shall remain fully liable for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors.
**7. Data Security**

Vendor shall implement and maintain SOC 2 Type II controls, encryption of Customer Data at rest and in transit, access controls, and logging and monitoring, as further described in Section 6.4 of the Agreement.
**8. Data Breach Notification**
Vendor shall notify Customer of any confirmed or reasonably suspected Security Breach within seventy-two (72) hours of discovery, in accordance with Section 6.5 of the Agreement.
**9. Data Subject Rights**

Vendor shall assist Customer in responding to data subject requests, including requests for access, deletion, correction, and portability, to the extent applicable under CCPA/CPRA or other applicable law.
**10. Data Return and Deletion**

Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement, Vendor shall return or delete all Customer Data in accordance with Section 6.7 of the Agreement within thirty (30) days of Customer\'s written request, and shall certify such return or deletion in writing.
**11. Audit Rights**

Customer shall have the right to audit Vendor\'s data processing activities, including review of SOC 2 Type II reports, upon reasonable notice, no more than once per Contract Year (unless a Security Breach has occurred, in which case Customer may conduct an additional audit).
**12. International Data Transfers**
Vendor shall not transfer Customer Data outside the United States without Customer\'s prior written consent.
**13. Term.** This DPA shall be coterminous with the Agreement. Data processing obligations shall survive as set forth in Section 6.7 of the Agreement.\]

Initial deposit within thirty (30) days of the Effective Date. Updates within thirty (30) days of material changes and no less frequently than quarterly.
**4. Release Conditions**
As set forth in Section 5A.3 of the Agreement: (a) insolvency; (b) material uncured breach exceeding sixty (60) days; (c) cessation of Platform support.
**5. Post-Release License**
Non-exclusive, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide license per Section 5A.3 of the Agreement.
**6. Verification.** Annual verification right per Section 5A.5 of the Agreement.

Vendor\'s responsibility per Section 5A.4 of the Agreement.

State of Delaware.

Civ. Part 314); (c) the California Financial Information Privacy Act (Cal. Fin. Code § 4050 *et seq.*); (d) any other applicable state consumer privacy statutes; and (e) all regulations, guidance, and opinions issued by competent regulatory authorities interpreting any of the foregoing, in each case as amended, superseded, or replaced from time to time.

Civ. Code § 1798.140(v). 111: **5.1 General Security Obligation.** Vendor shall implement and maintain appropriate Technical and Organizational Measures to protect Personal Information against unauthorized or unlawful Processing and against accidental loss, destruction, damage, alteration, or disclosure.
