Vendor shall ensure that such measures provide a level of security appropriate to the sensitivity of the Personal Information being Processed.
112: 
113: **5.2 Specific Security Requirements.** Without limiting the generality of Section 5.1, Vendor shall implement and maintain the following security measures at a minimum:
114: 
115: > \(a\) **Encryption at Rest.** All Personal Information stored by Vendor, whether on Vendor\'s own systems or on systems operated by Sub-Processors, shall be encrypted at rest using Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) with a key length of 256 bits (AES-256) or an equivalent or stronger encryption standard approved by Company in writing.
116: >
117: > \(b\) **Encryption in Transit.** All Personal Information transmitted by Vendor, including transmission over public networks, internal networks, and between Vendor and Sub-Processors, shall be encrypted in transit using Transport Layer Security (TLS) version 1.2 or higher, or an equivalent or stronger encryption protocol approved by Company in writing.
118: >
119: > \(c\) **Access Controls.** Vendor shall implement and maintain role-based access controls (RBAC) and adhere to the principle of least privilege, ensuring that access to Personal Information is limited to those personnel who require such access to perform their job functions in connection with the services under the Agreement. Access rights shall be reviewed and updated on a regular basis, and no less frequently than quarterly.
120: >
121: > \(d\) **Multi-Factor Authentication.** Vendor shall require multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all users accessing systems, applications, or environments that Process Personal Information, including remote access, administrative access, and access to cloud-based services.
122: >
123: > \(e\) **Vulnerability Assessments and Penetration Testing.** Vendor shall conduct regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing of its systems and infrastructure that Process Personal Information. Vulnerability assessments shall be conducted at least quarterly, and penetration testing shall be conducted at least annually by a qualified independent third party. Vendor shall provide Company with executive summaries of such assessments and tests upon request, along with remediation plans for any identified vulnerabilities rated as critical or high severity.
124: >
125: > \(f\) **Intrusion Detection and Monitoring.** Vendor shall implement and maintain intrusion detection systems (IDS) and intrusion prevention systems (IPS) to monitor network traffic and detect potential security threats to systems that Process Personal Information. Vendor shall maintain a security operations function capable of monitoring and responding to security alerts on a continuous, 24/7 basis.
126: >
127: > \(g\) **Logging and Audit Trails.** Vendor shall maintain comprehensive logging and audit trails for all access to, and actions performed on, Personal Information, including user authentication, data access, data modification, and data deletion events. Logs shall be maintained in a tamper-evident manner and retained for a period of not less than twelve (12) months, or such longer period as required by Applicable Data Protection Laws. Logs shall be made available to Company upon reasonable request and in connection with audits conducted under Article 12.
128: 
129: **5.3 SOC 2 Type II Certification.** Vendor shall obtain and maintain a current Service Organization Control (SOC) 2 Type II report, prepared by an independent certified public accounting firm in accordance with the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) Trust Services Criteria, covering at a minimum the Security, Availability, and Confidentiality trust services criteria. Vendor shall provide a copy of the most recent SOC 2 Type II report to Company upon execution of this DPA, and thereafter on an annual basis within thirty (30) days of Vendor\'s receipt of each updated report. Vendor shall promptly notify Company of any material exceptions, qualifications, or findings of non-compliance identified in any SOC 2 Type II report, along with Vendor\'s plans and timelines for remediation.
130: 
131: **5.4 Notification of Material Security Changes.** Vendor shall promptly notify Company in writing of any material changes to its Technical and Organizational Measures that may adversely affect the security, confidentiality, integrity, or availability of Personal Information. Such notification shall be provided at least thirty (30) days in advance of the planned change, or as soon as reasonably practicable in the case of emergency changes. Company reserves the right to review and approve or reject any such changes, and Vendor shall not implement any material adverse change without Company\'s prior written consent.
132: 
133: **5.5 Additional Security Specifications.** \[**\_\_\_**\] *(This field is reserved for engagement-specific security requirements to be mutually agreed upon by the Parties and documented herein or in a separately executed addendum. Such additional requirements, if any, shall be incorporated herein by reference and shall have the same force and effect as the security obligations set forth in this Article 5.)*
134: 
135: **[Article 6 --- CCPA Service Provider Certification]{.underline}**
136: 
137: **6.1 Understanding and Compliance Certification.** Vendor hereby certifies that it understands and will comply with the restrictions, obligations, and requirements applicable to service providers under the CCPA, as amended by the CPRA, and as set forth in this DPA. Vendor acknowledges that compliance with the CCPA is an essential component of its obligations under this DPA and the Agreement.
138: 
139: **6.2 Statutory Service Provider Certification.** In accordance with the requirements of Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag) and the regulations promulgated thereunder, Vendor hereby certifies each of the following:
140: 
141: > \(a\) Vendor certifies that it shall not sell or share Personal Information received from Company, and Vendor has no actual knowledge that it sells or shares Personal Information received from Company;
142: >
143: > \(b\) Vendor certifies that it shall not retain, use, or disclose Personal Information received from Company for any purpose other than for the specific Business Purposes set forth in the Agreement and this DPA, including retaining, using, or disclosing Personal Information for a commercial purpose other than providing the services specified in the Agreement, and as permitted under the CCPA and CPRA;
144: >
145: > \(c\) Vendor certifies that it shall not retain, use, or disclose Personal Information received from Company outside of the direct business relationship between Vendor and Company, except as expressly permitted by the CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(e)(6), or as otherwise authorized in writing by Company; and
146: >
147: > \(d\) Vendor certifies that it shall comply with all applicable provisions of the CCPA and CPRA, including all regulations promulgated by the California Privacy Protection Agency, as they may be amended from time to time.
148: 
149: **6.3 Company\'s Right to Ensure Compliance.** Vendor grants Company the right, upon reasonable notice, to take reasonable and appropriate steps to help ensure that Vendor uses Personal Information received from Company in a manner consistent with Company\'s obligations under the CCPA and CPRA. Such steps may include, without limitation, requesting information about Vendor\'s Processing activities, conducting audits or assessments in accordance with Article 12, and requiring Vendor to implement additional safeguards or remedial measures. Vendor shall cooperate fully with Company in connection with any such steps.
150: 
151: **6.4 Notification of Inability to Comply.** Vendor shall promptly notify Company if Vendor determines that it can no longer meet its obligations under the CCPA or CPRA, or if any change in Applicable Data Protection Laws materially affects Vendor\'s ability to comply with its obligations under this Article. Upon receipt of such notification, Company shall have the right to take reasonable and appropriate steps to stop and remediate any unauthorized use of Personal Information, which may include directing Vendor to cease Processing Personal Information, suspending the transfer of Personal Information to Vendor, and/or terminating the Agreement or the affected services thereunder. Vendor shall bear all costs and expenses associated with Vendor\'s failure to comply with its obligations under this Article.
152: 
153: **[Article 7 --- GLBA Safeguards Compliance]{.underline}**
154: 
155: **7.1 Applicability.** To the extent that Vendor receives, maintains, or Processes Personal Information that constitutes \"customer information\" or \"Nonpublic Personal Information\" as defined under GLBA and its implementing regulations, Vendor shall comply with the safeguards requirements of the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314) and any other applicable GLBA requirements. The obligations set forth in this Article 7 are in addition to, and do not limit, the security obligations set forth in Article 5.
156: 
157: **7.2 Comprehensive Information Security Program.** Vendor shall develop, implement, and maintain a comprehensive written information security program that contains administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to: (a) ensure the security and confidentiality of Nonpublic Personal Information; (b) protect against any anticipated threats or hazards to the security or integrity of such information; and (c) protect against unauthorized access to or use of such information that could result in substantial harm or inconvenience to any Consumer. The safeguards shall be appropriate to the size and complexity of Vendor\'s operations, the nature and scope of Vendor\'s activities, and the sensitivity of the Nonpublic Personal Information at issue.
158: 
159: **7.3 Designated Qualified Individual.** Vendor shall designate a qualified individual responsible for overseeing, implementing, and enforcing Vendor\'s information security program. The qualified individual may be an employee, affiliate, or a third-party service provider, provided that, in the case of a third-party service provider, Vendor retains overall responsibility for oversight and direction of the information security program. Vendor shall provide Company with the name, title, and contact information of the designated qualified individual upon Company\'s request.
160: 
161: **7.4 Periodic Risk Assessments.** Vendor shall conduct periodic risk assessments, no less frequently than annually, that: (a) identify reasonably foreseeable internal and external risks to the security, confidentiality, and integrity of Nonpublic Personal Information that could result in the unauthorized disclosure, misuse, alteration, destruction, or other compromise of such information; (b) assess the sufficiency of any safeguards in place to control these risks; and (c) design and implement safeguards to control the risks identified through the risk assessment. Vendor shall adjust its information security program based on the results of each risk assessment and shall maintain documentation of each risk assessment and the resulting actions taken.
162: 
163: **7.5 Access Restriction.** Vendor shall restrict access to Nonpublic Personal Information to those authorized personnel who have a legitimate business need for such access in connection with the services provided under the Agreement. Vendor shall implement and maintain procedures for granting, modifying, and revoking access to Nonpublic Personal Information, including prompt revocation of access upon termination of employment or engagement of any authorized personnel.
164: 
165: **7.6 Evidence of Compliance.** Vendor shall provide evidence of its compliance with the GLBA Safeguards requirements set forth in this Article upon Company\'s reasonable request. Such evidence may include, without limitation: (a) copies of or summaries of Vendor\'s information security program; (b) results of risk assessments (which may be provided in summary or redacted form to protect Vendor\'s confidential security information); (c) evidence of security training and awareness programs; (d) certifications or attestation letters from Vendor\'s designated qualified individual; and (e) any relevant audit reports, including SOC 2 Type II reports. Vendor shall provide such evidence within thirty (30) days of Company\'s request.
166: 
167: **[Article 8 --- Data Breach Notification]{.underline}**
168: 
169: **8.1 Notification Obligation.** Vendor shall notify Company of any confirmed or reasonably suspected Data Breach involving Personal Information Processed by Vendor or its Sub-Processors on behalf of Company without undue delay and in no event later than seventy-two (72) hours after Vendor first becomes aware of such Data Breach. Vendor shall direct its notification to Company\'s Privacy Contact identified in Section 14.8, as well as any other contacts designated by Company for Data Breach notifications. Notification shall be made by telephone and confirmed in writing via email and, if available, through any incident management portal designated by Company.
170: 
171: **8.2 Content of Notification.** Vendor\'s notification to Company under Section 8.1 shall include, to the extent known at the time of notification and without unreasonable delay:
172: 
173: > \(a\) A description of the nature of the Data Breach, including the categories and approximate number of Consumers affected and the categories and approximate number of Personal Information records affected;
174: >
175: > \(b\) The name, title, telephone number, and email address of Vendor\'s designated point of contact from whom Company may obtain additional information regarding the Data Breach;
176: >
177: > \(c\) A description of the likely consequences of the Data Breach, including a preliminary assessment of the risk of harm to affected Consumers;
178: >
179: > \(d\) A description of the measures taken or proposed to be taken by Vendor to address the Data Breach, including measures to contain the breach, mitigate its effects, and prevent recurrence; and
180: >
181: > \(e\) Any other information that Company may reasonably require to evaluate the Data Breach and fulfill its obligations under Applicable Data Protection Laws.
182: 
183: If Vendor does not have complete information at the time of the initial notification, Vendor shall provide the information described above in phases without further undue delay, and shall supplement its initial notification as additional information becomes available.
184: 
185: **8.3 Ongoing Cooperation.** Vendor shall cooperate fully with Company in investigating, remediating, and responding to any Data Breach, including: (a) providing Company with updated information regarding the Data Breach as it becomes available; (b) assisting Company in identifying affected Consumers and the Personal Information compromised; (c) supporting Company\'s regulatory filings, Consumer notifications, and other response activities; (d) preserving and producing documents, records, and other materials relevant to the Data Breach investigation; and (e) making Vendor\'s personnel, systems, and facilities reasonably available to Company and its investigators, legal counsel, and forensic consultants.
186: 
187: **8.4 Containment and Remediation.** Upon becoming aware of a Data Breach, Vendor shall immediately take all reasonable and necessary steps to contain, investigate, and remediate the Data Breach, including: (a) isolating affected systems; (b) preserving forensic evidence; (c) identifying the root cause; (d) eradicating the threat; (e) restoring the integrity of affected systems and data; and (f) implementing measures to prevent recurrence. All such containment, investigation, and remediation activities shall be performed at Vendor\'s sole cost and expense.
188: 
189: **8.5 Notification Restrictions.** Vendor shall not notify any Consumer, regulatory authority, law enforcement agency, credit reporting agency, or any other third party of a Data Breach involving Company\'s Personal Information without Company\'s prior written consent, unless Vendor is required to make such notification under Applicable Data Protection Laws, in which case Vendor shall: (a) notify Company of such legal requirement prior to making the notification, to the extent permitted by law; (b) coordinate with Company regarding the timing, content, and method of such notification; and (c) provide Company with a copy of any notification prior to its issuance, to the extent practicable.
190: 
191: **8.6 Preservation of Records and Evidence.** Vendor shall preserve all records, logs, files, data, communications, and other evidence related to a Data Breach in a secure and tamper-evident manner. Vendor shall not alter, destroy, or dispose of any such evidence without Company\'s prior written consent. Vendor shall make all such records and evidence available to Company and its authorized representatives upon request, at no additional cost to Company.
192: 
193: **8.7 Non-Exclusivity of Notification Obligations.** Vendor\'s notification obligations under this Article 8 are in addition to, and do not replace, modify, or limit, any notification obligations that Vendor may have under Applicable Data Protection Laws, the Agreement, or any other contractual arrangement between the Parties. Vendor shall comply with all notification obligations imposed by Applicable Data Protection Laws, including any obligations to notify regulatory authorities or affected individuals within the timeframes prescribed by law.
194: 
195: **[Article 9 --- Data Subject / Consumer Rights Cooperation]{.underline}**
196: 
197: **9.1 Assistance with Consumer Requests.** Vendor shall assist Company in fulfilling its obligations to respond to Consumer rights requests under Applicable Data Protection Laws, including but not limited to requests to know, access, correct, delete, port, and opt out of the sale or sharing of Personal Information, as well as requests to limit the use and disclosure of sensitive personal information. Vendor shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational processes to enable Company to comply with such Consumer requests in a timely and efficient manner.
198: 
199: **9.2 Notification of Direct Consumer Requests.** Vendor shall promptly, and in no event later than five (5) business days after receipt, notify Company if Vendor receives a Consumer rights request directly from a Consumer relating to Personal Information Processed on behalf of Company. Vendor shall not independently respond to, fulfill, or deny any such Consumer request unless directed to do so by Company in writing. Vendor shall refer the Consumer to Company for handling of the request, unless Company instructs otherwise.
200: 
201: **9.3 Systems and Processes for Consumer Requests.** Vendor shall maintain systems and processes capable of identifying, locating, retrieving, and, where applicable, deleting or correcting Personal Information by Consumer, in order to enable Company to respond to Consumer rights requests in compliance with the timeframes established by Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor shall ensure that its systems are designed to facilitate compliance with Company\'s obligations to respond to Consumer requests within forty-five (45) calendar days of receipt (or such other period as may be specified by Applicable Data Protection Laws), taking into account any extensions permitted by law.
202: 
203: **9.4 Identity Verification.** Vendor shall implement reasonable measures to verify the identity of Consumers submitting rights requests, in coordination with Company and in accordance with Company\'s identity verification procedures. Vendor shall not fulfill any Consumer request unless the identity of the requesting Consumer has been verified to Company\'s reasonable satisfaction. Vendor shall cooperate with Company in implementing and refining identity verification processes as needed.
204: 
205: **9.5 No Additional Fees.** Vendor shall not charge Company additional fees, surcharges, or other costs for assistance with Consumer rights requests that are part of Vendor\'s ordinary-course obligations under Applicable Data Protection Laws and this DPA. The Parties acknowledge that Vendor\'s obligation to assist with Consumer rights requests is an integral component of the services provided under the Agreement and is included in the fees paid by Company under the Agreement.
206: 
207: **[Article 10 --- De-Identification Standards]{.underline}**
208: 
209: **10.1 De-Identification Requirements.** If Vendor de-identifies Personal Information as part of the services provided under the Agreement, Vendor shall ensure that the de-identification process meets all requirements of Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m), and any other applicable statutory or regulatory definitions of de-identification, including the GLBA de-identification requirements where applicable. Vendor shall document its de-identification methodologies and make such documentation available to Company upon request.
210: 
211: **10.2 Technical Safeguards Against Re-Identification.** Vendor shall implement and maintain technical safeguards and business processes that are reasonably designed to prevent re-identification of De-Identified Data, including without limitation: (a) the removal or transformation of direct identifiers; (b) the suppression or generalization of quasi-identifiers to levels that prevent re-identification; (c) the application of appropriate statistical disclosure limitation techniques; and (d) access controls and use restrictions specific to De-Identified Data.
212: 
213: **10.3 Prohibition on Re-Identification.** Vendor shall not attempt to re-identify De-Identified Data, and shall contractually prohibit its Sub-Processors, employees, contractors, and agents from attempting to re-identify De-Identified Data. In the event that Vendor or any of its Sub-Processors, employees, contractors, or agents inadvertently re-identifies any De-Identified Data, Vendor shall: (a) immediately cease use of the re-identified data; (b) promptly notify Company; and (c) delete or re-de-identify the data in accordance with Company\'s instructions.
214: 
215: **10.4 Independent Verification.** Vendor shall subject any de-identification methodology to independent verification by a qualified professional (such as a statistician, data scientist, or privacy engineer with relevant expertise) before deploying such methodology in production. Vendor shall provide Company with a summary of the independent verification, including the methodology used, the conclusions reached, and any limitations identified, upon Company\'s request.
216: 
217: **10.5 Public Commitment.** Vendor shall make publicly available, such as in its privacy policy or on its website, a commitment to maintain and use De-Identified Data only in de-identified form and to not attempt to re-identify the data, as required by Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m) and any other Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor shall provide Company with a link to or copy of such public commitment upon request.
218: 
219: **10.6 Sub-Processor Obligations.** Any contractual obligations regarding De-Identified Data imposed on Sub-Processors engaged by Vendor shall be no less protective than those set forth in this Article 10. Vendor shall ensure that all Sub-Processors comply with the de-identification standards, technical safeguards, and prohibitions on re-identification set forth herein.
220: 
221: **[Article 11 --- Data Return and Deletion upon Termination]{.underline}**
222: 
223: **11.1 Data Return or Deletion.** Upon the expiration or termination of the Agreement (for any reason), or upon Company\'s earlier written request at any time during the term of the Agreement, Vendor shall, at Company\'s sole election, either: (a) return to Company all Personal Information in Vendor\'s possession or control, in a commonly used, structured, machine-readable format designated by Company, including all copies, backups, archives, and replications of Personal Information; or (b) securely delete and destroy all Personal Information in Vendor\'s possession or control, including all copies, backups, archives, and replications, using methods that render the Personal Information permanently unrecoverable. Company shall communicate its election to Vendor in writing.
224: 
225: **11.2 Timeframe for Return or Deletion.** Vendor shall complete the return or secure deletion and destruction of all Personal Information within thirty (30) days of receiving Company\'s instruction under Section 11.1. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to complete such return or deletion as promptly as practicable within such period. If Vendor requires additional time due to the volume or complexity of the data, Vendor shall notify Company in writing, specifying the additional time needed and the reasons therefor, and the Parties shall agree in writing on a revised timeline.
226: 
227: **11.3 Certification of Deletion or Return.** Upon completion of the return or deletion of Personal Information, Vendor shall provide Company with a written certification, signed by an authorized officer of Vendor, confirming that: (a) all Personal Information has been returned or deleted in accordance with Company\'s instructions and this DPA; (b) no copies, backups, archives, or replications of Personal Information remain in Vendor\'s possession or control, except as permitted under Section 11.4; and (c) Vendor has directed all Sub-Processors to comply with the data return and deletion obligations set forth in this Article. Vendor shall provide such certification within ten (10) business days of completing the return or deletion.
228: 
229: **11.4 Retention Exception.** Notwithstanding the foregoing, Vendor may retain Personal Information only to the extent that retention is required by Applicable Data Protection Laws, and only for the duration and purposes required by such laws. In the event Vendor retains any Personal Information pursuant to this Section 11.4, Vendor shall: (a) promptly notify Company in writing, identifying the specific Personal Information retained, the legal basis for retention, and the anticipated duration of retention; (b) continue to protect such retained Personal Information in accordance with the terms of this DPA; (c) limit Processing of such Personal Information to the purposes required by law; and (d) securely delete and destroy such Personal Information promptly upon the expiration of the applicable retention period.
230: 
231: **11.5 Sub-Processor Compliance.** Vendor shall ensure that all Sub-Processors comply with the data return and deletion obligations set forth in this Article 11. Vendor shall include in its Sub-Processor agreements provisions requiring Sub-Processors to return or delete Personal Information in accordance with Vendor\'s instructions, and Vendor shall obtain written certifications from Sub-Processors confirming compliance with such obligations.
232: 
233: **[Article 12 --- Audit and Inspection Rights]{.underline}**
234: 
235: **12.1 Information Availability.** Vendor shall make available to Company, upon reasonable request, all information reasonably necessary to demonstrate Vendor\'s compliance with this DPA and Applicable Data Protection Laws. Such information may include, without limitation, policies and procedures, training records, security assessment results, Data Breach records, Sub-Processor agreements, SOC 2 Type II reports, and other relevant documentation.
236: 
237: **12.2 Right to Conduct Audits.** Company, or its authorized third-party auditor (subject to reasonable confidentiality obligations acceptable to Vendor and not being a competitor of Vendor), shall have the right to conduct audits and inspections of Vendor\'s Processing activities, facilities, systems, and records related to the Processing of Personal Information under this DPA. Company shall provide Vendor with at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of any planned audit, specifying the scope, duration, and personnel involved. Vendor and Company shall cooperate in good faith to agree on the timing and logistics of any audit to minimize disruption to Vendor\'s operations.
238: 
239: **12.3 Frequency of Audits.** Audits may be conducted no more than once per calendar year, unless: (a) a Data Breach involving Company\'s Personal Information has occurred; (b) Company has reasonable grounds to believe that Vendor is materially non-compliant with this DPA or Applicable Data Protection Laws; or (c) an audit or investigation is required or requested by a regulatory authority with jurisdiction over Company or Vendor. In any of the circumstances described in clauses (a) through (c), Company may conduct additional audits as reasonably necessary, upon reasonable notice to Vendor, which notice may be shorter than the thirty (30) days specified in Section 12.2 in the case of urgent circumstances.
