12: 
13: **[1. Platform Overview]{.underline}**
14: 
15: **1.1 Product Description**
16: 
17: **MeridianIQ** is a cloud-hosted large-language-model document processing engine purpose-built for financial services and mortgage lending workflows. Published and maintained by Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC (\"Meridian\"), the platform delivers automated extraction, classification, validation, and structuring of unstructured and semi-structured loan origination documents using a proprietary fine-tunable LLM architecture.
18: 
19: MeridianIQ addresses a critical operational bottleneck in the mortgage lifecycle: the manual review, indexing, and data entry associated with the high volume and wide variety of documents generated during loan origination, underwriting, and closing. By automating these processes at the model level, MeridianIQ enables customers to reduce processing time, improve data accuracy, and free human reviewers to focus on exception handling and quality assurance rather than routine data extraction tasks.
20: 
21: The platform\'s target customer profile includes mortgage lenders, loan servicers, fintech platforms, and banks requiring high-throughput document intelligence at scale. MeridianIQ is designed to integrate seamlessly into existing loan origination systems (LOS), point-of-sale platforms, and servicing technologies via a well-documented RESTful API, enabling customers to embed intelligent document processing directly into their production workflows without disrupting existing system architectures.
22: 
23: **1.2 Supported Document Classes**
24: 
25: MeridianIQ provides out-of-the-box support for the following core document classes commonly encountered in residential mortgage origination and servicing workflows:
26: 
27: > • **Uniform Residential Loan Application (URLA / Fannie Mae Form 1003):** Full extraction of borrower, co-borrower, property, employment, income, asset, liability, and declarations data fields as defined by the current URLA specification, including the redesigned form effective March 2021 and subsequent revisions.
28: >
29: > • **Income and Employment Verification Documents:** Comprehensive extraction support for W-2 forms (all boxes and employer information), 1099 variants (1099-MISC, 1099-NEC, 1099-INT, 1099-DIV, 1099-R), pay stubs (gross pay, net pay, YTD earnings, deductions, pay period information), Verification of Employment (VOE) letters, and IRS tax transcripts (Form 4506-T responses, Wage and Income Transcripts, Tax Return Transcripts).
30: >
31: > • **Residential Appraisal Reports:** Extraction of property characteristics, comparable sales data, adjustments, and appraised value from Uniform Residential Appraisal Reports (URAR / Fannie Mae Form 1004) and common variants including Form 1073 (Individual Condominium Unit Appraisal Report), Form 1025 (Small Residential Income Property Appraisal Report), and desktop appraisal formats.
32: >
33: > • **Title Commitment Letters and Title Insurance Policies:** Extraction of commitment number, effective date, proposed insured, property legal description, Schedule A (coverage and policy amounts), Schedule B-I (requirements), and Schedule B-II (exceptions) from standard ALTA and regional title commitment and policy formats.
34: >
35: > • **Closing Disclosures (TRID):** Full extraction of all data fields from the TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure (TRID) Closing Disclosure form and Loan Estimate form, including loan terms, projected payments, costs at closing, summaries of transactions, loan calculations, and contact information sections.
36: 
37: Additional document classes beyond the standard set listed above are available through customer-specific fine-tuning engagements. During the implementation phase, Meridian works with the customer to identify additional document types relevant to the customer\'s workflows and trains custom adapter layers to support extraction from those formats. Common examples of customer-specific document classes include bank statements, asset verification letters, flood certifications, homeowners insurance declarations pages, and investor-specific stacking order checklists.
38: 
39: **1.3 Key Capabilities**
40: 
41: MeridianIQ provides the following core capabilities across all supported document classes:
42: 
43: **Document Classification and Routing.** Upon ingestion, MeridianIQ automatically classifies each document page or multi-page document into one of the supported document classes (or a customer-defined class, if applicable). Classification confidence scores are returned alongside the label, enabling downstream systems to apply routing logic---for example, directing low-confidence classifications to a human review queue while processing high-confidence documents straight through.
44: 
45: **Field-Level Data Extraction with Confidence Scoring.** The platform extracts individual data fields from each classified document and returns a per-field confidence score on a scale of 0.00 to 1.00. Confidence scores allow customer systems to implement threshold-based automation rules: fields exceeding a customer-defined confidence threshold can be accepted automatically, while fields falling below the threshold can be flagged for human review. This approach provides a tunable balance between automation throughput and data quality.
46: 
47: **Cross-Document Data Reconciliation and Consistency Checks.** When multiple documents are submitted as part of a single loan file or batch, MeridianIQ performs cross-document reconciliation to identify discrepancies between data extracted from different sources. For example, the platform can flag inconsistencies between borrower income reported on the URLA and income reflected on submitted W-2 forms, or between the property address on the appraisal report and the closing disclosure. Reconciliation results are returned as part of the structured output, with specific discrepancy codes and descriptions.
48: 
49: **Regulatory Compliance Flagging.** MeridianIQ includes built-in compliance validation logic aligned to key regulatory requirements applicable to mortgage lending. The platform checks for TRID field completeness and consistency on Closing Disclosure and Loan Estimate documents, validates ECOA-required data field presence, and assesses HMDA field completeness to support the customer\'s regulatory reporting obligations. Compliance flags are returned in the extraction output with references to the applicable regulatory requirement, enabling customers to address potential compliance gaps prior to loan closing or delivery.
50: 
51: **Structured JSON Output for Downstream Integration.** All extraction results, classification labels, confidence scores, reconciliation findings, and compliance flags are returned in a structured JSON format designed for direct consumption by downstream systems such as loan origination systems, data warehouses, underwriting engines, and quality control platforms. The JSON schema is fully documented and versioned, and Meridian provides schema migration guidance when breaking changes are introduced in new API versions.
52: 
53: **[2. Architecture]{.underline}**
54: 
55: **2.1 Model Architecture**
56: 
57: MeridianIQ is built on a proprietary transformer architecture utilizing an encoder-decoder design that has been pre-trained on a large, curated corpus of financial services documents. This base model has been specifically optimized for the characteristics of mortgage and lending documentation, including multi-column layouts, handwritten annotations, scanned image artifacts, inconsistent formatting across document originators, and the domain-specific vocabulary and regulatory terminology common in the financial services industry.
58: 
59: **Base Model.** The base model\'s parameter count and detailed architectural specifications are available under NDA upon request. At a high level, the encoder processes the visual and textual representation of each document page---incorporating both OCR-derived text and spatial layout information---while the decoder generates structured extraction outputs conditioned on the encoded representation and the target extraction schema for the classified document type.
60: 
61: **Fine-Tuning Framework.** MeridianIQ employs a modular adapter layer architecture based on Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) principles. This approach enables customer-specific customization without modifying the underlying base model weights. During the implementation engagement, Meridian trains adapter layers on customer-provided labeled document sets to adapt the model\'s extraction behavior to the customer\'s specific document formats, terminology, field naming conventions, and extraction schemas. Because the base model weights remain frozen during adapter training, this approach is computationally efficient, preserves the base model\'s generalized document understanding capabilities, and ensures that customer-specific customizations do not interfere with other tenants\' adapter configurations.
62: 
63: **Adapter Layer Architecture.** Each customer\'s adapter weights are stored independently and applied dynamically at inference time. When a document is submitted for processing, the inference pipeline identifies the appropriate tenant and loads the corresponding adapter weights atop the frozen base model. This design allows Meridian to maintain a single base model version across all tenants while delivering customer-specific extraction performance. Adapter weights are versioned, and customers can maintain multiple adapter versions (e.g., for A/B testing or staged rollouts) simultaneously.
64: 
65: **Inference Pipeline.** The end-to-end inference pipeline proceeds through the following stages:
66: 
67: 1\. **Document Ingestion:** The submitted document file is received via the API, validated for format and size compliance, and queued for processing.
68: 
69: 2\. **Pre-Processing (OCR / Layout Analysis):** The document undergoes optical character recognition (for image-based inputs) and layout analysis to extract text content, spatial coordinates, table structures, and page segmentation information. Meridian utilizes a proprietary OCR engine optimized for financial document quality, supplemented by layout analysis models that identify headers, footers, tables, form fields, and free-text regions.
70: 
71: 3\. **Classification:** The pre-processed document representation is passed through the classification stage, which assigns a document class label and confidence score.
72: 
73: 4\. **Extraction via Base Model + Adapter:** The classified document is processed by the base model with the tenant\'s applicable adapter weights loaded, producing raw extraction outputs for each target field in the document class schema.
74: 
75: 5\. **Post-Processing and Validation:** Raw extraction outputs are subjected to post-processing rules including format normalization (e.g., date formatting, currency standardization, SSN masking), cross-field consistency checks, and business rule validations. Confidence scores are calibrated during this stage.
76: 
77: 6\. **Structured Output:** The final extraction results, classification label, confidence scores, reconciliation findings, and compliance flags are assembled into the structured JSON response payload and returned to the customer via the API or webhook callback.
78: 
79: **2.2 Deployment Options**
80: 
81: MeridianIQ is available in two deployment configurations, allowing customers to select the option that best aligns with their operational requirements, regulatory posture, and budget.
82: 
83: **2.2.1 Multi-Tenant SaaS (Standard).** The standard deployment option hosts the customer\'s workloads on shared compute infrastructure with logical tenant isolation enforced at every layer of the stack. Data segregation is maintained at the application layer (tenant-scoped API authentication and authorization), the storage layer (tenant-partitioned database schemas and isolated object storage buckets), and the network layer (security group and network policy enforcement). Each tenant\'s adapter weights are stored in isolated, encrypted object storage containers that are accessible only by the inference pipeline processes operating on behalf of that specific tenant.
84: 
85: The multi-tenant SaaS deployment is suitable for the majority of production workloads and provides the fastest time-to-value, as environment provisioning is streamlined and infrastructure management is handled entirely by Meridian. Customers benefit from shared infrastructure efficiencies, including automatic scaling, platform-level patching and updates, and Meridian\'s operational monitoring and incident response processes.
86: 
87: **2.2.2 Dedicated Instance.** For customers with regulatory requirements mandating physical infrastructure isolation, or for customers whose internal information security policies require single-tenant environments, Meridian offers a dedicated instance deployment option. Under this model, single-tenant compute and storage infrastructure is provisioned within Meridian\'s cloud environment exclusively for the customer\'s use. Dedicated instances operate on isolated virtual private cloud (VPC) infrastructure with dedicated compute resources, and no other customer\'s workloads share the underlying hardware or network environment.
88: 
89: The dedicated instance option is available at additional cost; pricing is determined based on the customer\'s throughput requirements, compute resource allocation, storage volume, and support tier, and is provided upon request. Dedicated instances also support enhanced security configurations including customer-managed encryption keys (CMK), mutual TLS (mTLS) for API authentication, and private network connectivity via AWS PrivateLink.
90: 
91: Meridian recommends the dedicated instance option for customers subject to specific regulatory mandates concerning data residency, physical infrastructure isolation, or heightened data security requirements that cannot be satisfied by logical isolation alone.
92: 
93: **[3. Infrastructure]{.underline}**
94: 
95: **3.1 Hosting Environment**
96: 
97: MeridianIQ\'s production infrastructure is hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS), leveraging AWS\'s extensive security certifications, global infrastructure footprint, and managed services ecosystem.
98: 
99: **Primary Region:** US East (N. Virginia) --- \`us-east-1\`. The primary region hosts all production workloads under normal operating conditions, including the API gateway, inference fleet, database tier, object storage, and supporting microservices.
100: 
101: **Failover Region:** US West (Oregon) --- \`us-west-2\`. The failover region maintains a warm standby of all critical platform components and receives continuous data replication from the primary region.
102: 
103: **Failover Architecture:** MeridianIQ employs an active-passive failover architecture with automated DNS-based failover. In the event of a primary region outage, automated health checks trigger DNS failover to the secondary region. The platform is engineered to achieve a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of less than one (1) minute and a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of less than fifteen (15) minutes under standard failure conditions. These targets reflect the continuous replication architecture and pre-provisioned standby resources in the failover region, though actual recovery times may vary depending on the nature and scope of the failure event.
104: 
105: **Compute Resources:** Inference workloads are executed on GPU-accelerated instances, specifically AWS EC2 P-series (for high-throughput, compute-intensive inference) and Inf-series (for cost-optimized inference at scale) instances. Meridian continuously evaluates and adopts newer instance types as they become available to optimize inference performance and cost efficiency.
106: 
107: **3.2 Availability & Redundancy**
108: 
109: MeridianIQ\'s infrastructure is designed for high availability across all tiers of the platform stack:
110: 
111: **Multi-Availability-Zone Deployment.** All production components within each region are deployed across multiple AWS Availability Zones (AZs). Each AZ consists of one or more physically separated data centers with independent power, cooling, and networking. This architecture ensures that the failure of a single AZ does not result in platform unavailability.
112: 
113: **Auto-Scaling Inference Fleet.** The GPU-accelerated inference fleet is configured with auto-scaling policies that dynamically adjust compute capacity based on real-time demand signals including request queue depth, GPU utilization, and latency metrics. A minimum baseline capacity is reserved per tenant to ensure consistent performance during traffic spikes and to prevent resource contention between tenants on the multi-tenant deployment.
114: 
115: **Load Balancing.** Incoming API traffic is distributed across the inference fleet via AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) with health-check-based routing. The ALB continuously monitors the health of backend inference instances and automatically removes unhealthy instances from the target group, redistributing traffic to healthy instances without interruption to the customer.
116: 
117: **Database Tier.** The platform\'s relational data store is Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, configured with synchronous multi-AZ replication. Aurora automatically maintains a synchronous replica in a separate Availability Zone, providing automatic failover with minimal data loss in the event of a primary database instance failure. Aurora\'s storage layer replicates data six ways across three AZs, providing additional durability.
118: 
119: **3.3 Disaster Recovery**
120: 
121: Meridian maintains a comprehensive disaster recovery program to ensure business continuity and data durability in the event of a regional outage or catastrophic failure:
122: 
123: **Continuous Replication.** All tenant data---including processed documents, extraction results, configuration data, and adapter weights---is continuously replicated from the primary region (\`us-east-1\`) to the failover region (\`us-west-2\`). Replication is performed at both the database level (Aurora cross-region replication) and the object storage level (S3 cross-region replication), ensuring that the failover region maintains a near-real-time copy of all critical data.
124: 
125: **Quarterly DR Failover Tests.** Meridian conducts full disaster recovery failover tests on a quarterly basis to validate the reliability of the failover architecture, confirm that RPO and RTO targets are achievable under realistic conditions, and identify any gaps or improvements needed in the DR process. Test reports, including observed RPO and RTO metrics, are available to customers upon written request.
126: 
127: **Backup Retention.** Database snapshots are retained on a 30-day rolling basis, providing point-in-time recovery capability for the most recent 30-day window. Object storage items---including adapter weights, pipeline artifacts, and processed document outputs---are retained for 90 days in both the primary and failover regions. Backup encryption is consistent with the platform\'s data-at-rest encryption standards described in Section 6.1.
128: 
129: **[4. API Specifications]{.underline}**
130: 
131: **4.1 General.** MeridianIQ exposes a RESTful HTTPS API as the primary interface for all document submission, processing, extraction retrieval, and platform management operations. The API is designed to be intuitive for developers familiar with modern REST conventions and follows consistent patterns across all endpoints.
132: 
133: > • **Protocol:** RESTful API served exclusively over HTTPS. All HTTP (non-TLS) connections are rejected.
134: >
135: > • **Base URL Format:** \`https://api.meridianiq.com/v2/{tenant*id}/\` --- where \`{tenant*id}\` is the unique identifier assigned to the customer during onboarding.
136: >
137: > • **Data Format:** All request and response payloads are formatted as JSON.
138: >
139: > • **Character Encoding:** UTF-8 is used for all text data in request and response payloads.
140: >
141: > • **API Versioning:** The API is versioned via the URI path (e.g., \`/v1/\`, \`/v2/\`). When a new API version is released, the prior version enters a deprecation period. Meridian provides a minimum of twelve (12) months of continued support for deprecated API versions following issuance of a formal sunset notice, giving customers adequate time to migrate their integrations to the current version.
142: 
143: **4.2 Authentication & Authorization**
144: 
145: All API requests must be authenticated and authorized before processing. MeridianIQ implements industry-standard OAuth 2.0 for API authentication and fine-grained scope-based authorization.
146: 
147: > • **Authentication Method:** OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant. Customers are issued a \`client*id\` and \`client*secret\` during onboarding, which are used to obtain short-lived access tokens from the token endpoint.
148: >
149: > • **Token Endpoint:** \`https://auth.meridianiq.com/oauth2/token\`
150: >
151: > • **Access Token Lifetime:** 3,600 seconds (one hour) by default. The token lifetime is configurable on a per-tenant basis upon request to accommodate customer-specific security policies.
152: >
153: > • **Authorization Scopes:** Access tokens are issued with one or more of the following scopes, which control the operations the bearer is permitted to perform:
154: >
155: > • \`documents:read\` --- Retrieve document processing status, extraction results, and document metadata.
156: >
157: > • \`documents:write\` --- Submit documents and batch jobs for processing.
158: >
159: > • \`extraction:execute\` --- Trigger extraction operations on previously submitted documents.
160: >
161: > • \`models:manage\` --- View and manage adapter configurations, including listing adapters and retrieving adapter performance metrics.
162: >
163: > • \`admin:config\` --- Access tenant administration and configuration settings, including webhook configuration, retention policy settings, and user management.
164: >
165: > • **Mutual TLS (mTLS):** For customers on the dedicated instance deployment, mutual TLS authentication is available as an additional security layer. When mTLS is enabled, the client must present a valid X.509 certificate during the TLS handshake in addition to providing a valid OAuth 2.0 access token. This provides two-factor authentication at the transport layer and is recommended for environments with heightened security requirements.
166: 
167: **4.3 Core Endpoints**
168: 
169: The following table summarizes the core API endpoints available in MeridianIQ API v2. Detailed endpoint documentation, including request/response schemas, parameter descriptions, error codes, and example payloads, is provided in the MeridianIQ API Developer Guide, which is furnished to customers during onboarding.
170: 
171:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
172:   **Endpoint**                                **Method**              **Description**
173:   ------------------------------------------- ----------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
174:   \`/documents\`                              POST                    Submit one or more documents for processing. Accepts multipart/form-data or base64-encoded document payloads. Returns a document identifier (\`doc_id\`) and initial processing status.
175: 
176:   \`/documents/{doc_id}\`                     GET                     Retrieve the current processing status and summary results for a previously submitted document, identified by \`doc_id\`.
177: 
178:   \`/documents/{doc_id}/extraction\`          GET                     Retrieve the full structured extraction output for a completed document, including all extracted fields, confidence scores, classification label, reconciliation results, and compliance flags.
179: 
180:   \`/batch\`                                  POST                    Submit a batch processing job containing multiple documents. Returns a batch identifier (\`batch_id\`) and initial batch status.
181: 
182:   \`/batch/{batch_id}\`                       GET                     Retrieve the current status of a batch processing job, including per-document status within the batch, overall progress percentage, and completion estimates.
183: 
184:   \`/models/adapters\`                        GET                     List all adapter configurations available to the tenant, including adapter identifiers, version numbers, associated document classes, and training dates.
185: 
186:   \`/models/adapters/{adapter_id}/metrics\`   GET                     Retrieve performance metrics for a specific adapter, including F1 score, precision, recall, and throughput statistics from the most recent evaluation cycle.
187: 
188:   \`/health\`                                 GET                     Platform health and status check endpoint. Returns the current operational status of the API, inference pipeline, and dependent services. Suitable for integration into customer health monitoring and alerting systems.
189:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
190: 
191: **4.4 Rate Limits**
192: 
193: To ensure consistent performance and fair resource allocation across all tenants, MeridianIQ enforces the following rate limits on API requests:
194: 
195: > • **Standard Tier Rate Limit:** 500 requests per second per tenant. This limit applies to all API endpoints in aggregate.
196: >
197: > • **Burst Allowance:** Tenants may temporarily exceed the standard rate limit up to 750 requests per second for intervals not exceeding 30 seconds in duration. Burst capacity accommodates short-lived traffic spikes without requiring pre-provisioned rate limit increases.
198: >
199: > • **Rate Limit Response Headers:** Every API response includes the following headers to enable client-side rate limit awareness and management:
200: >
201: > • \`X-RateLimit-Limit\` --- The maximum number of requests permitted per second under the tenant\'s current rate limit.
202: >
203: > • \`X-RateLimit-Remaining\` --- The number of requests remaining in the current rate limit window.
204: >
205: > • \`X-RateLimit-Reset\` --- The UTC epoch timestamp at which the rate limit window resets.
206: >
207: > • **Rate Limit Exceeded Behavior:** When a tenant exceeds the applicable rate limit (including burst allowance), the API returns an HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) response. The response includes a \`Retry-After\` header indicating the number of seconds the client should wait before retrying the request. Clients are expected to implement appropriate backoff logic in their integration code to handle rate limit responses gracefully.
208: 
209: Higher rate limits are available for customers with enterprise agreements and may be negotiated based on documented throughput requirements.
210: 
211: **4.5 Payload Specifications**
212: 
213: The following specifications govern the size, format, and content constraints for API request and response payloads:
214: 
215: > • **Maximum Single-Document File Size:** 50 MB. Documents exceeding this size limit will be rejected with an HTTP 413 (Payload Too Large) response.
216: >
217: > • **Supported Input Formats:** PDF, TIFF, PNG, JPEG, and DOCX. Documents submitted in unsupported formats will be rejected with an HTTP 415 (Unsupported Media Type) response.
218: >
219: > • **Maximum Pages Per Document:** 500 pages. Documents exceeding this page limit will be rejected at the pre-processing stage, and the processing status will reflect the rejection reason.
220: >
221: > • **Batch Job Maximum:** 1,000 documents per batch request. Batch jobs exceeding this limit will be rejected with an appropriate error response. Customers requiring larger batch sizes should contact their account representative to discuss batch segmentation strategies or provisioned capacity increases.
222: >
223: > • **Response Payload Structure:** All extraction responses are returned as JSON objects containing the following top-level elements:
224: >
225: > • Extraction fields: key-value pairs for each extracted data field, organized by document section and field name as defined in the document class schema.
226: >
227: > • Confidence scores: a numeric value between 0.00 and 1.00 for each extracted field, representing the model\'s confidence in the accuracy of the extracted value.
228: >
229: > • Document classification label: the assigned document class and classification confidence score.
230: >
231: > • Processing metadata: timestamps, processing duration, model version, adapter version, and pipeline stage details.
232: 
233: **4.6 Webhooks.** For asynchronous processing workflows (which represent the recommended integration pattern for production deployments), MeridianIQ supports configurable webhook callbacks that notify the customer\'s system when document or batch processing is complete.
234: 
235: **Webhook Configuration.** Customers configure one or more webhook endpoint URLs via the administrative console or the \`/admin/webhooks\` API endpoint. Webhook endpoints must be HTTPS and must respond with an HTTP 2xx status code to acknowledge receipt of the webhook payload.
236: 
237: **Webhook Payload Signing.** All webhook payloads are signed using HMAC-SHA256 with a customer-specific secret that is generated during webhook configuration and shared securely with the customer. The signature is included in the \`X-Meridian-Signature\` header of the webhook HTTP request. Customers should validate the signature on every incoming webhook to verify authenticity and prevent tampering.
238: 
239: **Retry Policy.** If the customer\'s webhook endpoint fails to respond with an HTTP 2xx status code (or fails to respond within 30 seconds), MeridianIQ will retry delivery using an exponential backoff schedule. The platform will attempt up to five (5) retries over a 24-hour period. If all retries are exhausted without successful delivery, the webhook event is logged as undeliverable, and the customer can retrieve the processing results via the standard polling endpoints (\`/documents/{doc*id}\` and \`/batch/{batch*id}\`).
240: 
241: **[5. Standard Service Level Parameters]{.underline}**
242: 
243: This section describes the standard service level parameters that Meridian publishes for the MeridianIQ platform. These parameters represent Meridian\'s baseline commitments and are subject to the terms and conditions of the executed customer agreement. Customers seeking enhanced or customized SLA terms should engage with their Meridian account representative to discuss enterprise SLA options.
244: 
245: **5.1 Availability. Monthly Uptime Commitment: 99.9%**
246: 
247: Meridian commits to maintaining a monthly uptime percentage of at least 99.9% for the MeridianIQ API, as measured and calculated in accordance with the methodology described below.
248: 
249: **Uptime Calculation:**
250: 
251: > Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total minutes in calendar month − Downtime minutes) ÷ Total minutes in calendar month) × 100
252: 
253: **Downtime Definition.** \"Downtime\" is defined as any period of five (5) or more consecutive minutes during which the MeridianIQ API returns HTTP 5xx server error responses or is unreachable (i.e., fails to respond to properly formed requests) as measured by Meridian\'s external synthetic monitoring system. Meridian\'s synthetic monitoring agents issue health check requests to the API from geographically distributed external monitoring points at one-minute intervals. Intermittent errors lasting less than five consecutive minutes, or isolated request failures that do not constitute a sustained outage, are not counted as Downtime.
254: 
255: **Exclusions from Downtime Calculation.** The following events and periods are excluded from the Downtime calculation and do not count against the monthly uptime commitment:
256: 
257: > • **Scheduled Maintenance Windows:** Planned maintenance periods that are communicated to customers at least seventy-two (72) hours in advance via email notification and the platform status page. Meridian will schedule maintenance during low-traffic periods (typically Saturday or Sunday, 2:00 AM -- 6:00 AM Eastern Time) to the extent practicable. Total scheduled maintenance will not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month under normal circumstances.
258: >
259: > • **Force Majeure Events:** Events beyond Meridian\'s reasonable control, as defined in the applicable customer agreement, including but not limited to natural disasters, acts of war or terrorism, government actions, pandemics, and widespread utility or telecommunications failures.
260: >
261: > • **Customer-Caused Downtime:** Unavailability or errors resulting from the customer\'s systems, networks, code, configurations, or actions, including misconfigured API calls, exhausted rate limits, expired authentication tokens, or customer-side network outages.
262: >
263: > • **External Infrastructure Failures:** DNS resolution failures, internet backbone routing failures, or other network connectivity issues outside of Meridian\'s controlled infrastructure and network perimeter.
264: 
265: **5.2 Latency. Response Latency Target: p95 ≤ 600 ms**
266: 
267: Meridian targets a 95th percentile (p95) end-to-end response latency of six hundred (600) milliseconds or less for synchronous single-document extraction API calls, measured from the MeridianIQ API gateway\'s receipt of the inbound request to the dispatch of the response from the API gateway.
268: 
269: This published standard SLA parameter of p95 ≤ 600 ms establishes the vendor\'s baseline capability for production inference workloads across all supported document classes. It reflects the performance characteristics of the inference pipeline under typical production conditions, including document classification, extraction via the base model and adapter, post-processing, and response serialization.
270: 
271: **Measurement Basis.** The latency target applies to synchronous single-document extraction calls (i.e., requests to the \`/documents\` endpoint processed in synchronous mode). Batch processing jobs submitted via the \`/batch\` endpoint are excluded from the latency target, as batch jobs are processed asynchronously and are subject to different throughput and scheduling dynamics.
272: 
273: **Measurement Point.** Latency is measured at Meridian\'s API gateway---specifically, from the timestamp of request ingress at the gateway to the timestamp of response egress from the gateway. This measurement excludes network transit time between the customer\'s systems and Meridian\'s API endpoint, as network latency is influenced by factors outside Meridian\'s control, including the customer\'s geographic location, network provider, and internet routing conditions.
274: 
275: **Reporting.** Latency percentile metrics---including p50 (median), p90, p95, and p99---are available to customers in two formats:
276: 
277: > • **Real-Time Dashboard:** Accessible via the MeridianIQ web console and the \`/metrics\` API endpoint, providing near-real-time visibility into current and historical latency performance.
278: >
279: > • **Monthly SLA Reports:** Meridian generates and delivers monthly SLA performance reports to each customer, summarizing uptime, latency, and accuracy metrics for the reporting period.
280: 
281: **5.3 Model Accuracy**
282: 
283: **Standard Accuracy Target: F1 Score ≥ 0.90 on Standard Document Classes**
284: 
285: Meridian targets a field-level F1 score of 0.90 or higher on each of the standard document classes listed in Section 1.2, as evaluated against Meridian\'s held-out benchmark dataset.
286: 
287: **Evaluation Methodology.** The accuracy target is expressed as an F1 score, which is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, computed at the individual extracted field level. This metric balances the model\'s ability to correctly extract values that are present in the document (recall) with its ability to avoid extracting incorrect values (precision). The evaluation is performed against Meridian\'s held-out benchmark dataset, which consists of a representative sample of documents across each supported document class, labeled by Meridian\'s annotation team and subject to quality assurance review.
288: 
289: **Benchmark Refresh.** The benchmark dataset is refreshed on a semi-annual basis to ensure that it remains representative of the current document formats, layouts, and data distributions encountered in production. Methodology documentation describing the benchmark composition, labeling standards, and evaluation protocol is provided to customers upon request.
290: 
291: **Customer-Specific Adapter Accuracy.** For customer-specific adapters trained during the implementation engagement, accuracy is measured against a customer-provided labeled validation set rather than Meridian\'s internal benchmark. Performance targets for fine-tuned adapters---including F1, precision, and recall thresholds---are established collaboratively during the implementation engagement and formally documented in the applicable Statement of Work. Because adapter performance depends on factors including the volume and quality of the customer\'s training data, the consistency of the customer\'s document formats, and the complexity of the target extraction schema, adapter-specific accuracy targets may differ from the standard platform-level target.
292: 
293: **Accuracy Metrics Availability.** Adapter-level accuracy metrics are accessible via the \`/models/adapters/{adapter_id}/metrics\` API endpoint and are included in the monthly performance reports delivered to the customer. Metrics include F1 score, precision, recall, and per-field accuracy breakdowns for each document class covered by the adapter.
294: 
295: **5.4 Standard SLA Credit Schedule**
296: 
297: In the event that Meridian fails to meet the monthly uptime commitment of 99.9% as described in Section 5.1, the customer is eligible for service credits in accordance with the following schedule:
298: 
299:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
300:   **Monthly Uptime Percentage**       **Service Credit (% of Monthly Fees)**
301:   ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------
302:   99.0% -- \< 99.9%                   5%
303: 
304:   95.0% -- \< 99.0%                   10%
305: 
306:   \< 95.0%                            15%
307:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
308: 
309: **Credit Application.** Service credits are applied as a reduction against the fees invoiced in the next billing period following the month in which the uptime shortfall occurred. Credits are not redeemable for cash, are not transferable, and may not be carried forward beyond one billing period.
310: 
311: **Sole and Exclusive Remedy.** Under Meridian\'s standard terms, service credits as described in this schedule are the customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy for Meridian\'s failure to meet the monthly uptime commitment. This limitation applies unless otherwise specified in the executed customer agreement.
312: 
313: **Enhanced SLA Options.** For customers requiring more stringent commitments or additional remedies, Meridian offers enhanced SLA tiers under negotiated enterprise agreements. Enhanced options may include latency-specific credits (e.g., credits for failure to meet the p95 latency target), accuracy-specific credits (e.g., credits for failure to meet F1 score targets on standard document classes), higher uptime commitments (e.g., 99.95% or 99.99%), and increased credit percentages. Customers interested in enhanced SLA terms should contact their Meridian account representative.
314: 
315: **[6. Data Handling & Security]{.underline}**
316: 
317: Meridian maintains a comprehensive information security program designed to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of customer data processed by the MeridianIQ platform. The following sections describe the key technical controls implemented across the platform.
318: 
319: **6.1 Encryption. Data at Rest.** All customer data stored by the MeridianIQ platform---including submitted documents, extraction results, configuration data, and adapter weights---is encrypted at rest using AES-256 encryption. Encryption keys are managed via AWS Key Management Service (KMS), which provides centralized key management, automatic key rotation, and comprehensive audit logging of all key usage events. For customers on the dedicated instance deployment, a customer-managed key (CMK) option is available, allowing the customer to maintain control over the encryption key lifecycle within their own AWS KMS account while Meridian\'s platform uses the customer\'s key for encryption and decryption operations.
320: 
321: **Data in Transit.** All data transmitted to and from the MeridianIQ API, as well as all internal service-to-service communication within the platform, is encrypted in transit using Transport Layer Security (TLS). TLS 1.3 is the preferred protocol and is enforced on all API endpoints. TLS 1.2 is accepted as a fallback for clients that do not yet support TLS 1.3. Earlier TLS versions (1.1, 1.0) and SSL are not supported and connections attempting to negotiate these protocols will be rejected. Cipher suite selection prioritizes forward-secrecy-capable cipher suites in accordance with industry best practices.
322: 
323: **Adapter Weight Encryption.** Customer-specific adapter weights are encrypted at rest with tenant-specific encryption keys, ensuring that even in the event of unauthorized access to the underlying storage infrastructure, adapter weights cannot be decrypted without the corresponding tenant-specific key.
324: 
325: **6.2 Data Isolation**
326: 
327: Meridian enforces strict data isolation between tenants to prevent unauthorized access to or leakage of customer data:
328: 
329: **Logical Tenant Isolation.** On the multi-tenant SaaS deployment, tenant isolation is enforced at the application layer (tenant-scoped authentication, authorization, and data access controls), the network layer (security groups, network ACLs, and optionally VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink for private connectivity), and the storage layer (tenant-partitioned database schemas and isolated object storage containers).
330: 
331: **No Cross-Tenant Training.** Customer document data is never used for training or fine-tuning models for other customers. Each customer\'s data is used exclusively for the purpose of providing the MeridianIQ service to that customer, including training and evaluating that customer\'s adapter layers. This commitment is a foundational element of Meridian\'s data handling policy and is reflected in the Data Processing Addendum executed with each customer.
332: 
333: **No Data Commingling.** Customer document data is not commingled in storage or processing pipelines with other tenants\' data. Even on the multi-tenant deployment where compute resources are shared, document data flows through tenant-scoped processing queues and is stored in tenant-isolated storage containers at every stage of the pipeline.
334: 
335: **6.3 Data Retention & Deletion**
336: 
337: **Retention Period.** Processed documents and extraction results are retained for the period specified in the customer\'s executed agreement. In the absence of a customer-specified retention period, the default retention period is ninety (90) days following processing completion. Upon expiration of the retention period, data is queued for secure deletion.
338: 
339: **Secure Deletion.** Data deletion is performed in accordance with the guidelines set forth in NIST Special Publication 800-88, *Guidelines for Media Sanitization*. For data stored on encrypted media (which includes all customer data on the MeridianIQ platform), cryptographic erasure---the destruction of the encryption key rendering the encrypted data unrecoverable---is the primary deletion method. Customers may also request immediate deletion of specific documents or all tenant data at any time during the term of the agreement by submitting a written request to Meridian\'s support team.
340: 
341: **Adapter Weight Retention.** Customer-specific adapter weights are retained for the duration of the customer agreement to ensure continuous service delivery. Upon termination or expiration of the customer agreement, adapter weights are securely deleted within thirty (30) days, unless the customer and Meridian agree in writing to an alternative disposition (e.g., export of adapter weights to the customer, if technically feasible and contractually permitted).
342: 
343: **6.4 Access Controls**
344: 
345: **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).** The MeridianIQ platform implements role-based access control for all tenant administration and API access operations. Customer administrators can define roles with granular permissions aligned to the OAuth 2.0 scopes described in Section 4.2, and assign those roles to individual users or API credentials. This allows customers to enforce the principle of least privilege within their MeridianIQ tenant.
346: 
347: **Meridian Personnel Access.** Access by Meridian personnel to customer environments and data is strictly limited to authorized support and engineering staff who require access to perform their job functions (e.g., troubleshooting customer-reported issues, performing platform maintenance, or conducting adapter training operations). All Meridian personnel access to customer environments is logged with detailed audit trails including the identity of the accessing individual, the timestamp, the resources accessed, and the actions performed. Access logs are retained in accordance with Meridian\'s information security policy and are available to customers upon request for audit purposes.
348: 
349: **Quarterly Access Reviews.** Meridian conducts quarterly reviews of all personnel access privileges to customer environments to ensure that access remains appropriate and that privileges are promptly revoked for personnel who no longer require access (e.g., due to role changes or employment termination).
350: 
351: **Privileged Access Controls.** Access to privileged administrative functions within the MeridianIQ platform infrastructure requires multi-factor authentication (MFA) and is provisioned on a just-in-time basis. Privileged access sessions are time-limited and automatically expire after a defined period, requiring re-authentication and re-authorization for continued access.
352: 
353: **[7. Compliance & Certifications]{.underline}**
354: 
355: **7.1 SOC 2 Type II**
356: 
357: Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC maintains a current SOC 2 Type II report issued in accordance with the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) Trust Services Criteria. The report covers the **Security**, **Availability**, and **Confidentiality** trust service criteria as they relate to the MeridianIQ platform and its supporting infrastructure and operational processes.
358: 
359: **Audit Period.** The most recent SOC 2 Type II report covers the twelve (12)-month period ending December 31, 2024.
360: 
361: **Auditor.** The audit was conducted by an independent third-party CPA firm with recognized expertise in information technology auditing and SOC reporting.
362: 
363: **Report Availability.** The SOC 2 Type II report is available to customers and prospective customers under a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) upon request. Customers may request a copy of the report by contacting their Meridian account representative or by emailing compliance@meridianiq.com. Meridian issues an updated SOC 2 Type II report annually and will notify customers when a new report is available.
364: 
365: **7.2 Additional Compliance Capabilities**
366: 
367: Beyond the SOC 2 Type II attestation, MeridianIQ has been designed and operated with the following regulatory and compliance considerations in mind:
368: 
369: **Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA).** The MeridianIQ platform is designed to support customers\' compliance with the safeguards requirements of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act when processing non-public personal information (NPPI). The platform\'s encryption, access control, data isolation, and audit logging capabilities are aligned to the administrative, technical, and physical safeguard requirements contemplated by the GLBA Safeguards Rule. Customers remain responsible for their own GLBA compliance programs, and Meridian\'s role as a service provider is governed by the terms of the executed customer agreement and Data Processing Addendum.
370: 
371: **CCPA / CPRA.** With respect to personal information processed on behalf of the customer, Meridian operates as a \"service provider\" as that term is defined under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and the California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA). Meridian processes personal information solely on behalf of and at the direction of the customer, and does not sell, share, or use personal information for any purpose other than providing the MeridianIQ service as described in the customer agreement. A Data Processing Addendum (DPA) reflecting Meridian\'s service provider obligations under the CCPA/CPRA is available and is executed as part of the customer agreement.
372: 
373: **NIST Cybersecurity Framework Alignment.** Meridian\'s information security program is aligned to the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework (CSF). Meridian has mapped its security controls to the NIST CSF functions (Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover) and sub-categories, and maintains this mapping as a living document that is updated as the platform and security program evolve. The NIST CSF control mapping is cross-referenced to the SOC 2 trust service criteria to provide a unified view of the company\'s control environment.
374: 
375: **Penetration Testing.** Meridian engages an independent third-party security firm to conduct a comprehensive penetration test of the MeridianIQ platform and its supporting infrastructure on an annual basis. The penetration test scope includes external network testing, web application testing (OWASP Top 10 coverage), API security testing, and authenticated testing of the platform\'s multi-tenant isolation controls. A summary of findings from the most recent penetration test is available to customers under NDA upon request. Critical and high-severity findings, if any, are remediated in accordance with Meridian\'s vulnerability management policy, and customers are notified of any findings that materially affect the security posture of the platform.
376: 
377: **7.3 Subprocessors.** Meridian utilizes a limited number of subprocessors in the delivery of the MeridianIQ service, including cloud infrastructure providers, monitoring and observability tool providers, and support tooling providers. A current list of subprocessors, including the name, location, and function of each subprocessor, is provided to customers upon request.
