**\"Uptime SLA\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 9.1.
**[ARTICLE 2 --- LICENSE GRANT AND SCOPE OF USE]{.underline}**
**Section 2.1 --- License Grant**

Subject to and conditioned upon Customer\'s compliance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including timely payment of all Fees, Vendor hereby grants to Customer a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable license during the Term to access and use the Platform solely for Customer\'s internal business operations in connection with Customer\'s lending technology product known as LendStream. The license granted hereunder includes the right to access and use the Platform through the APIs provided by Vendor, to submit Customer Data for processing through the Platform, and to receive and use the outputs generated by the Platform in connection with LendStream. This license is further conditioned on Customer\'s compliance with the Documentation and all applicable laws, rules, and regulations.
**Section 2.2 --- Scope of Authorized Use**

Customer may permit its employees, and authorized contractors who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in Article 7, to access and use the Platform on Customer\'s behalf and in furtherance of Customer\'s authorized use hereunder. Customer shall be responsible for all acts and omissions of its employees and authorized contractors in connection with their access to and use of the Platform. Use of the Platform is limited to the processing, analysis, and classification of Customer Data in support of LendStream\'s document processing workflows. Customer shall not use the Platform for any purpose other than as expressly authorized by this Agreement. Customer shall not exceed the Included API Calls in any Contract Year, except as subject to the overage charges set forth in Section 4.3.
**Section 2.3 --- Restrictions**
Customer acknowledges that the Platform and Base Model represent proprietary technology of Vendor. Customer shall not, and shall not permit any third party to:

> \(a\) reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, or otherwise attempt to derive the source code, algorithms, data structures, or underlying ideas of the Platform or the Base Model, except to the extent that such restriction is expressly prohibited by applicable law notwithstanding a contractual prohibition;

> \(b\) sublicense, sell, resell, lease, rent, loan, distribute, or otherwise make available the Platform or any component thereof to any third party, whether as a service bureau, managed service, or otherwise;

> \(c\) use the Platform or any output thereof for competitive benchmarking, competitive analysis, or to develop, train, or improve a product or service that competes with the Platform or any of Vendor\'s other products or services;
> \(d\) remove, obscure, alter, or deface any proprietary notices, labels, or marks on or in the Platform, the Documentation, or any output thereof;

> \(e\) access the Platform other than through the APIs and access mechanisms provided by Vendor, including without limitation by scraping, crawling, or using any automated means not expressly authorized by Vendor;

> \(f\) attempt to extract, reconstruct, distill, or reverse engineer model weights, architectures, training data, or any other proprietary components from the Platform, whether through prompt injection, model inversion, membership inference, or any other technique; or

> \(g\) use the Platform in any manner that violates applicable law or regulation, or that infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates the Intellectual Property Rights or other rights of any third party.
**Section 2.4 --- Reservation of Rights**

Except for the limited license expressly granted in Section 2.1, Vendor reserves all rights in and to the Platform, including all Intellectual Property Rights therein. No implied licenses are granted under this Agreement by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Customer\'s right to access and use the Platform is limited to the express license grant set forth in Section 2.1, and all other rights are expressly reserved by Vendor. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to grant Customer any right to access the source code or model weights of the Platform or the Base Model.
**[ARTICLE 3 --- IMPLEMENTATION AND TRAINING SERVICES]{.underline}**
**Section 3.1 --- Implementation Services**

Vendor shall perform the Implementation Services as described in the initial Statement of Work attached hereto as Exhibit A (the \"**Initial SOW**\") and any additional Statements of Work that may be executed by the Parties from time to time pursuant to this Article 3. The Implementation Services under the Initial SOW shall include, without limitation: (a) provisioning and configuration of Customer\'s dedicated Platform environment; (b) API integration of the Platform with Customer\'s LendStream product; (c) fine-tuning of the Base Model using Customer Data to optimize the Platform\'s performance for Customer\'s specific document processing requirements; (d) initial accuracy validation and testing of the fine-tuned model; and (e) initial training of Customer\'s designated personnel on the use and operation of the Platform. All Implementation Services shall be performed by Vendor personnel who are qualified and experienced in the relevant subject matter.
**Section 3.2 --- Implementation Milestones**
The Implementation Services shall be performed in accordance with the following milestones, as further described in Exhibit A:

> **Milestone 1 --- SOW Execution.** Execution of the Initial SOW by both Parties. Achievement of Milestone 1 shall trigger payment of the first installment of the Implementation Fee as set forth in Section 4.2(a).

> **Milestone 2 --- Go-Live.** Successful achievement of Go-Live, targeted for October 1, 2025, at which point the Platform shall be made available for production use by Customer. Achievement of Milestone 2 shall trigger payment of the second installment of the Implementation Fee as set forth in Section 4.2(b). Go-Live shall be conditioned upon the Platform performing materially in accordance with the Documentation, as mutually confirmed by the Parties through the acceptance process described in Exhibit A.

Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve the targeted Go-Live date, but the targeted Go-Live date is an estimate only and shall not constitute a guaranteed delivery date. Delays caused by Customer\'s failure to fulfill its cooperation obligations under Section 3.3 shall extend the targeted Go-Live date by a commensurate period.
**Section 3.3 --- Customer Cooperation**

Customer acknowledges that Vendor\'s ability to perform the Implementation Services is dependent upon Customer\'s timely cooperation and assistance. Customer shall provide reasonable cooperation in connection with the Implementation Services, including without limitation: (a) timely provision of Customer Data in the format and quality reasonably specified by Vendor; (b) access to Customer\'s systems and environments as reasonably necessary for Vendor to perform API integration and testing; (c) designation of qualified Customer personnel with appropriate subject matter expertise to serve as points of contact and to participate in the implementation process, including providing timely feedback and approvals; and (d) such other cooperation as may be reasonably requested by Vendor and described in the applicable Statement of Work. Customer\'s failure to provide timely cooperation may result in delays in the Implementation Services, and Vendor shall not be responsible for any such delays to the extent caused by Customer\'s failure to perform its cooperation obligations under this Section 3.3.
**Section 3.4 --- Change Orders**

Any changes to the scope, timeline, deliverables, or fees for Implementation Services shall be documented in a mutually agreed written change order signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. No change to the Implementation Services shall be binding unless set forth in a duly executed change order. Each change order shall specify the nature of the change, any impact on the project timeline and milestones, and any additional fees associated with the change. Vendor shall not be obligated to perform any work outside the scope of an executed Statement of Work or change order.
**[ARTICLE 4 --- FEES AND PAYMENT]{.underline}**
**Section 4.1 --- Annual Platform Fee**

In consideration of the license and access rights granted hereunder, Customer shall pay to Vendor an annual platform fee of Two Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,400,000) per Contract Year (the \"**Annual Platform Fee**\"). The Annual Platform Fee shall be invoiced by Vendor in equal monthly installments of Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$200,000) per month, with each monthly invoice due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice. Vendor shall issue monthly invoices on or about the first business day of each calendar month during the Term, beginning with the first calendar month following the Effective Date.
**Section 4.2 --- Implementation Fee**

In consideration of the Implementation Services described in Article 3 and Exhibit A, Customer shall pay to Vendor a one-time implementation and fine-tuning fee of Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$850,000) (the \"**Implementation Fee**\"). The Implementation Fee shall be payable in two (2) equal installments of Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000) each, as follows:

> \(a\) **First Installment.** Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000), due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice following execution of the Initial SOW (Milestone 1).
> \(b\) **Second Installment.** Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000), due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice following achievement of Go-Live (Milestone 2).
**Section 4.3 --- Overage Fees**

The Annual Platform Fee includes forty million (40,000,000) API calls per Contract Year (the \"**Included API Calls**\"). API calls made by Customer in excess of the Included API Calls during any Contract Year shall be invoiced by Vendor at a rate of twelve-thousandths of a dollar (\$0.012) per API call (the \"**Overage Rate**\"). Overage Fees shall be invoiced monthly in arrears, based on Vendor\'s metering and usage data for the applicable calendar month. Each such invoice shall include a summary of API call usage for the month, including the number of API calls consumed and the number of remaining Included API Calls for the applicable Contract Year. Overage Fee invoices shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice.
**Section 4.4 --- Taxes**

All Fees set forth in this Agreement are exclusive of any and all applicable taxes, duties, levies, or similar governmental charges (collectively, \"**Taxes**\"). Customer shall be responsible for, and shall pay, all sales, use, value-added, goods and services, withholding, and similar Taxes imposed on or in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, excluding taxes based on Vendor\'s net income, capital, or franchise taxes assessed against Vendor. If Vendor is required by law to collect any Taxes from Customer, Vendor shall include such Taxes on the applicable invoice and Customer shall remit payment of such Taxes together with the applicable Fees. If Customer is required to withhold any Taxes from amounts payable to Vendor, Customer shall gross up the payment so that Vendor receives the full amount of the invoiced Fees after deduction of such withholding Taxes.
**Section 4.5 --- Late Payments**

Any undisputed Fees not paid when due shall accrue interest at the lesser of (a) one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (18% per annum) or (b) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, from the date such payment was due until the date such payment is received in full by Vendor. In addition, Vendor may, upon at least fifteen (15) days\' prior written notice to Customer, suspend Customer\'s access to the Platform if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid for more than forty-five (45) days past its due date, and such suspension shall continue until all outstanding amounts, including accrued interest, have been paid in full. The foregoing remedies are in addition to, and not in lieu of, any other remedies available to Vendor under this Agreement or applicable law.
**Section 4.6 --- Total Contract Value**
For informational purposes and clarity, the total contract value for the Initial Term (exclusive of Overage Fees and Taxes) is as follows:
> \(a\) Annual Platform Fees for three (3) Contract Years: \$2,400,000 × 3 = **\$7,200,000**;
> \(b\) Implementation Fee (one-time): **\$850,000**;

The foregoing total contract value is an estimate for informational purposes only and does not include any Overage Fees, Taxes, or fees for additional Statements of Work that may be executed during the Term. The total contract value does not limit Vendor\'s right to invoice for Overage Fees or other amounts payable under this Agreement.
**[ARTICLE 5 --- INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY]{.underline}**
**Section 5.1 --- Vendor IP Ownership**

As between the Parties, Vendor is and shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to: (a) the Platform; (b) the Base Model; (c) all Fine-Tuned Weights; (d) all Customer-Trained Adaptations; (e) all Derivative Models; and (f) all improvements, enhancements, updates, upgrades, modifications, and derivative works of any of the foregoing, together with all Intellectual Property Rights therein and thereto, regardless of whether such items are created by Vendor independently, in collaboration with Customer, or through the processing of Customer Data. For the avoidance of doubt, all fine-tuned weights, adapter layers, prompt-tuning parameters, and similar derivative model parameters generated through the fine-tuning, training, or adaptation of the Base Model using Customer Data shall be considered Derivative Models and are owned exclusively by Vendor. Customer hereby assigns, and agrees to assign, to Vendor all right, title, and interest that Customer may have or acquire in any Derivative Models, Customer-Trained Adaptations, or Fine-Tuned Weights, including all Intellectual Property Rights therein, and agrees to execute such documents and take such further actions as may be reasonably necessary to effectuate and perfect such assignment.
**Section 5.2 --- Customer Data Ownership**

As between the Parties, Customer is and shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to all Customer Data, including all Intellectual Property Rights therein. Vendor\'s right to access, use, and process Customer Data is limited to the purposes expressly set forth in this Agreement, including providing the Platform, performing the Implementation Services, and the service improvement purposes described in Section 6.1. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as transferring ownership of Customer Data from Customer to Vendor. Vendor acknowledges that Customer Data may contain NPPI and other regulated data, and Vendor agrees to treat all Customer Data in accordance with its obligations under this Agreement and applicable law.
**Section 5.3 --- Feedback**

If Customer or any of its employees, contractors, or agents provides any suggestions, enhancement requests, ideas, recommendations, corrections, or other feedback regarding the Platform, the Documentation, or any of Vendor\'s products or services (collectively, \"**Feedback**\"), Customer hereby grants to Vendor a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid-up, transferable, sublicensable license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, create derivative works from, distribute, display, perform, and otherwise exploit such Feedback in any manner and for any purpose, without restriction, attribution, or compensation to Customer. Customer acknowledges that Vendor may use Feedback to improve the Platform, develop new features, or create new products or services, and that Vendor shall have no obligation to implement or incorporate any Feedback.
**Section 5.4 --- No Other Rights**

Except as expressly set forth in this Article 5 and the license granted in Section 2.1, neither Party grants the other Party any right, title, or interest in or to its Intellectual Property Rights, whether by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to grant Customer any rights in Vendor\'s trade secrets, proprietary algorithms, model architectures, training methodologies, or other confidential technical information, except as expressly provided herein.
**[ARTICLE 6 --- DATA PROCESSING AND PRIVACY]{.underline}**
**Section 6.1 --- Customer Data Processing**

Vendor shall process Customer Data solely for the following purposes: (a) providing the Platform and performing Vendor\'s obligations under this Agreement, including the Implementation Services; (b) operating, maintaining, supporting, and securing the Platform; and (c) service improvement purposes, including but not limited to improving the Base Model, developing new features and capabilities, training and validating Derivative Models, and conducting research and development related to Vendor\'s artificial intelligence products and services. For purposes of clause (c), Vendor may process Customer Data in de-identified and aggregated form such that the data does not identify or permit identification of Customer or any individual. Vendor shall implement appropriate technical measures to de-identify and aggregate Customer Data prior to its use for service improvement purposes. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data to any third party or use Customer Data for any purpose other than as expressly set forth in this Section 6.1.
**Section 6.2 --- Controller Status**

Each Party acknowledges that it acts as an independent data controller with respect to its own processing activities relating to Customer Data under this Agreement. Customer is the data controller with respect to Customer Data as it relates to Customer\'s internal business operations and its provision of Customer Data to Vendor. Vendor\'s processing of Customer Data for the purpose of providing the Platform under Section 6.1(a) and (b) shall be undertaken by Vendor on behalf of Customer. Vendor\'s processing of Customer Data for service improvement purposes under Section 6.1(c) shall be undertaken by Vendor as an independent data controller, and Vendor shall independently determine the purposes and means of such processing. Each Party shall be individually responsible for complying with its obligations under applicable data protection and privacy laws with respect to its processing activities as a data controller.
**Section 6.3 --- Compliance with Laws**

Each Party shall comply with all applicable data protection and privacy laws, rules, and regulations in connection with its processing of Customer Data under this Agreement, including without limitation: (a) the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 6801--6809, and its implementing regulations, including Regulation S-P (17 C.F.R. Part 248) and the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314) (\"**GLBA**\"), to the extent applicable to the processing of NPPI; (b) the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act of 2020, Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1798.100--1798.199.100 (\"**CCPA/CPRA**\"), to the extent applicable; and (c) any other applicable federal, state, or international data protection or privacy laws. To the extent required by applicable law, the Parties shall cooperate in good faith to enter into any additional data processing agreements or addenda necessary to comply with applicable data protection requirements.
**Section 6.4 --- Security Measures**

Vendor shall implement and maintain throughout the Term commercially reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect Customer Data against unauthorized access, acquisition, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction, consistent with industry standards for cloud-based enterprise software providers. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Vendor\'s security program shall include: (a) encryption of Customer Data in transit (using TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (using AES-256 or equivalent); (b) access controls, including multi-factor authentication, role-based access, and least-privilege principles; (c) regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing; (d) intrusion detection and prevention systems; (e) security incident response procedures; and (f) employee security awareness training. Vendor shall, upon Customer\'s reasonable request and no more than once per twelve (12)-month period, provide Customer with a summary of Vendor\'s then-current security measures and any SOC 2 Type II or equivalent audit reports covering Vendor\'s information security controls.
**Section 6.5 --- Data Breach Notification**

In the event of any confirmed security breach involving the unauthorized access, acquisition, use, or disclosure of Customer Data (a \"**Security Breach**\"), Vendor shall: (a) notify Customer of the Security Breach without unreasonable delay, and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours of confirmation of the Security Breach; (b) promptly investigate the Security Breach and take reasonable steps to contain, mitigate, and remediate the Security Breach; (c) provide Customer with reasonably detailed information regarding the nature and scope of the Security Breach, including the categories and approximate number of records affected, the likely consequences of the Security Breach, and the measures taken or proposed to address and mitigate the Security Breach; and (d) cooperate with Customer in Customer\'s investigation, response, and notification obligations in connection with the Security Breach. The obligations set forth in this Section 6.5 shall not be construed as an acknowledgment by Vendor of any fault or liability with respect to the Security Breach.
**Section 6.6 --- Return and Deletion of Data**

Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, Vendor shall, at Customer\'s written election made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration, either (a) return Customer Data to Customer in a commercially reasonable format designated by Customer, or (b) securely delete or destroy all Customer Data in Vendor\'s possession or control, including all copies, backups, and archives thereof. Vendor shall complete such return or deletion within sixty (60) calendar days of receipt of Customer\'s written request. Upon completion of the return or deletion, Vendor shall certify in writing to Customer that all Customer Data has been returned or deleted in accordance with this Section 6.6. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Vendor may retain copies of Customer Data to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, or legal hold obligation, provided that Vendor continues to protect such retained data in accordance with this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, data that has been de-identified and aggregated for service improvement purposes in accordance with Section 6.1 shall not constitute Customer Data for purposes of this Section 6.6 and shall not be subject to the return or deletion obligations set forth herein.
**[ARTICLE 7 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**
**Section 7.1 --- Definition of Confidential Information**

\"**Confidential Information**\" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the \"**Disclosing Party**\") to the other Party (the \"**Receiving Party**\") in connection with this Agreement, whether disclosed orally, in writing, electronically, or by any other means, and whether or not marked or designated as \"confidential,\" \"proprietary,\" or with any similar legend, that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Confidential Information includes: (a) business plans, strategies, forecasts, and financial information; (b) technical information, including source code, algorithms, model architectures, model weights, training data, APIs, and system designs; (c) trade secrets; (d) customer lists, supplier lists, and pricing information; (e) product roadmaps and development plans; and (f) the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including all pricing, fee, and commercial terms. Customer Data shall be deemed Confidential Information of Customer regardless of whether it is marked or designated as confidential.

Confidential Information shall not include information that: (i) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of or breach by the Receiving Party; (ii) was already known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records; (iii) is rightfully received by the Receiving Party from a third party without restriction on disclosure and without breach of any obligation of confidentiality owed to the Disclosing Party; or (iv) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records.
**Section 7.2 --- Obligations**

The Receiving Party shall: (a) hold the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information in strict confidence; (b) not disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to any third party except as expressly permitted under Section 7.3; (c) use the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information solely for the purposes of performing its obligations or exercising its rights under this Agreement; and (d) protect the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information using commercially reasonable measures that are at least as protective as those used by the Receiving Party to protect its own confidential information of a similar nature, but in no event less than a reasonable standard of care.

The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article 7 shall remain in effect during the Term and for a period of five (5) years following the expiration or termination of this Agreement; provided, however, that the confidentiality obligations with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law shall continue for so long as such information remains a trade secret.
**Section 7.3 --- Permitted Disclosures**

The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to its employees, officers, directors, agents, contractors, consultants, advisors, and Affiliates who have a legitimate need to know such information for the purposes of this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article 7 (collectively, \"**Authorized Recipients**\"). The Receiving Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Article 7 by its Authorized Recipients.

The Receiving Party may also disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, court order, subpoena, or other legal process, provided that the Receiving Party: (a) provides the Disclosing Party with prompt written notice of such requirement (to the extent legally permitted) so that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy; (b) cooperates with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party\'s expense, in seeking such protective order or other remedy; and (c) discloses only the minimum amount of Confidential Information necessary to comply with such requirement. Any Confidential Information disclosed pursuant to a legal compulsion shall retain its confidential status for all other purposes under this Agreement.
**[ARTICLE 8 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**
**Section 8.1 --- Mutual Representations and Warranties**
Each Party hereby represents and warrants to the other Party as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Effective Date that:
> \(a\) it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its formation;
> \(b\) it has full corporate or limited liability company power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to perform its obligations hereunder;
> \(c\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate or limited liability company action;

> \(d\) this Agreement constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity; and

> \(e\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement will not (i) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of any provision of such Party\'s organizational documents, (ii) violate any applicable law, rule, or regulation, or (iii) conflict with, result in a breach of, or constitute a default under any material agreement or instrument to which such Party is a party or by which it is bound.
**Section 8.2 --- Vendor Representations and Warranties**
Vendor hereby represents and warrants to Customer that:

> \(a\) the Platform, when used in accordance with the Documentation and this Agreement, will perform materially in accordance with the functional specifications set forth in the Documentation during the Term;

> \(b\) the Implementation Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, consistent with generally accepted industry standards for similar services, using personnel with the requisite skill, experience, and qualifications;

> \(c\) Vendor has all rights necessary to grant the license set forth in Section 2.1, free and clear of any liens, encumbrances, or restrictions that would materially impair Customer\'s exercise of the rights granted thereunder; and

> \(d\) to Vendor\'s knowledge as of the Effective Date, the Platform, as provided by Vendor and used in accordance with this Agreement, does not infringe any registered United States patent or registered United States copyright of any third party.

Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor\'s sole and exclusive liability, for any breach of the warranty set forth in Section 8.2(a) shall be for Vendor, at its option, to (i) repair or replace the non-conforming Platform functionality so that it conforms to the Documentation, or (ii) if Vendor is unable to repair or replace such functionality within a commercially reasonable period, terminate this Agreement and refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Fees attributable to the period following such termination.
**Section 8.3 --- Disclaimer**

EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 8, VENDOR MAKES NO WARRANTIES OF ANY KIND, WHETHER EXPRESS, IMPLIED, STATUTORY, OR OTHERWISE, WITH RESPECT TO THE PLATFORM, THE IMPLEMENTATION SERVICES, THE BASE MODEL, ANY DERIVATIVE MODELS, OR ANY OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION ANY WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, NON-INFRINGEMENT, TITLE, ACCURACY, COMPLETENESS, RELIABILITY, OR QUALITY OF OUTPUTS. VENDOR DOES NOT WARRANT THAT THE PLATFORM WILL BE ERROR-FREE, UNINTERRUPTED, OR FREE OF HARMFUL COMPONENTS, OR THAT THE OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM WILL BE ACCURATE, COMPLETE, OR SUITABLE FOR ANY PARTICULAR PURPOSE. CUSTOMER ACKNOWLEDGES THAT LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS ARE PROBABILISTIC IN NATURE AND THAT OUTPUTS MAY CONTAIN ERRORS, HALLUCINATIONS, OR INACCURACIES, AND CUSTOMER IS SOLELY RESPONSIBLE FOR EVALUATING AND VALIDATING ALL OUTPUTS FOR ITS INTENDED USE.
**[ARTICLE 9 --- SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDITS]{.underline}**
**Section 9.1 --- Uptime**

Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain Platform availability of at least ninety-nine and nine-tenths percent (99.9%) in any calendar month (the \"**Uptime SLA**\"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:
> **Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100**

For purposes of the Uptime SLA, \"**Downtime**\" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor\'s monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer\'s systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer\'s acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer\'s access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).
**Section 9.2 --- Latency**

Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain API response latency at or below six hundred (600) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 600 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor\'s internal monitoring systems at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.
**Section 9.3 --- Model Accuracy**

Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above zero point ninety (F1 ≥ 0.90), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset established during the implementation process. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer\'s production document processing workloads.
**Section 9.4 --- Service Credits**

In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA in any calendar month, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a \"**Service Credit**\"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the Uptime SLA failure occurred.

Service Credits constitute Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor\'s sole and exclusive liability, for any failure to meet the service level commitments set forth in this Article 9. Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against Customer\'s next invoice(s) under this Agreement and shall not be refundable in cash. In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed twenty percent (20%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year.
**Section 9.5 --- Reporting**

Vendor shall provide Customer with monthly reports detailing Platform uptime, API latency, and model accuracy metrics for the preceding calendar month. Such reports shall be delivered to Customer within ten (10) business days following the end of each calendar month. Reports shall include, at a minimum: (a) Platform availability percentage; (b) total Downtime minutes and the cause of each incident; (c) API latency at the 50th percentile (p50) and 95th percentile (p95); (d) model accuracy metrics, including F1 score, precision, and recall, as measured against the validation dataset; and (e) API call usage data, including the total number of API calls consumed during the month and the cumulative total for the current Contract Year. Vendor shall make authorized Customer personnel available for a monthly service review meeting, upon Customer\'s reasonable request, to discuss the monthly reports and any performance issues.
**[ARTICLE 10 --- LIMITATION OF LIABILITY]{.underline}**
**Section 10.1 --- Exclusion of Consequential Damages**

IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, PUNITIVE, OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO DAMAGES FOR LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF REVENUE, LOSS OF GOODWILL, LOSS OF DATA, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES, COST OF PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES, BUSINESS INTERRUPTION, OR ANY OTHER COMMERCIAL DAMAGES OR LOSSES, WHETHER ARISING UNDER CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER LEGAL OR EQUITABLE THEORY, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES OR COULD HAVE FORESEEN SUCH DAMAGES. THE FOREGOING EXCLUSION SHALL APPLY REGARDLESS OF WHETHER SUCH DAMAGES ARISE FROM BREACH OF CONTRACT, BREACH OF WARRANTY, TORT, OR ANY OTHER CAUSE OF ACTION.
**Section 10.2 --- Aggregate Liability Cap**

EXCEPT AS SET FORTH IN SECTION 10.3, EACH PARTY\'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, WHETHER ARISING UNDER CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER LEGAL OR EQUITABLE THEORY, SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES ACTUALLY PAID OR PAYABLE BY CUSTOMER TO VENDOR DURING THE SIX (6)-MONTH PERIOD IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE DATE OF THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM. FOR CLARITY, BASED ON THE ANNUAL PLATFORM FEE, THIS LIABILITY CAP EQUALS ONE MILLION TWO HUNDRED THOUSAND DOLLARS (\$1,200,000).
**Section 10.3 --- Exclusions from Cap**

The limitations and exclusions set forth in Sections 10.1 and 10.2 shall not apply to: (a) Customer\'s payment obligations under Article 4; (b) either Party\'s obligations under Article 7 (Confidentiality); (c) either Party\'s indemnification obligations under Article 11; (d) liability arising from a Party\'s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud; or (e) liability arising from Vendor\'s breach of Section 6.4 (Security Measures) or Section 6.5 (Data Breach Notification) to the extent involving Vendor\'s gross negligence or willful misconduct.
**[ARTICLE 11 --- INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**
**Section 11.1 --- Vendor Indemnification**

Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"**Customer Indemnitees**\") from and against any third-party claim, suit, action, or proceeding alleging that Customer\'s authorized use of the Platform in accordance with this Agreement constitutes direct infringement of a registered United States patent or a registered United States copyright (each, an \"**IP Claim**\"), and shall pay all damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) finally awarded by a court of competent jurisdiction or agreed to in settlement of such IP Claim.

Vendor\'s obligations under this Section 11.1 are expressly limited to claims of direct infringement of registered United States patents and registered United States copyrights. Vendor shall have no indemnification obligation with respect to any claim based on or arising from:
> \(i\) trade secrets, trademarks, service marks, trade dress, or unregistered intellectual property rights of any kind;
> \(ii\) indirect infringement, contributory infringement, or inducement of infringement;

> \(iii\) Customer\'s combination of the Platform with any third-party products, services, hardware, software, data, or content not provided by Vendor, to the extent such combination gives rise to the infringement claim;
> \(iv\) Customer\'s modification, alteration, or customization of the Platform or its outputs, to the extent such modification gives rise to the infringement claim;
> \(v\) Customer\'s use of the Platform in violation of this Agreement, the Documentation, or applicable law;
> \(vi\) Customer\'s use of a version of the Platform other than the then-current version, if the infringement would have been avoided by use of the then-current version made available by Vendor; or
> \(vii\) any output generated by the Platform, to the extent the infringement claim relates to the content of such output rather than the Platform itself.
**Section 11.2 --- Vendor Remediation**
If the Platform becomes, or in Vendor\'s reasonable opinion is likely to become, the subject of an IP Claim, Vendor may, at its sole option and expense:
> \(a\) procure for Customer the right to continue using the Platform under terms substantially consistent with this Agreement;

> \(b\) modify or replace the Platform (or the infringing component thereof) to make it non-infringing, provided that such modification or replacement does not materially diminish the functionality of the Platform; or

177: 177	(d) this Agreement constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors' rights generally and to general principles of equity; and
178: 178	(e) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement will not (i) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of any provision of such Party's organizational documents, (ii) violate any applicable law, rule, or regulation, or (iii) conflict with, result in a breach of, or constitute a default under any material agreement or instrument to which such Party is a party or by which it is bound.
179: 179	Section 8.2 — Vendor Representations and Warranties
180: 180	Vendor hereby represents and warrants to Customer that:
181: 181	(a) the Platform, when used in accordance with the Documentation and this Agreement, will perform materially in accordance with the functional specifications set forth in the Documentation during the Term;
182: 182	(b) the Implementation Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, consistent with generally accepted industry standards for similar services, using personnel with the requisite skill, experience, and qualifications;
183: 183	(c) Vendor has all rights necessary to grant the license set forth in Section 2.1, free and clear of any liens, encumbrances, or restrictions that would materially impair Customer's exercise of the rights granted thereunder; 
184: 184	(d)  Customer's authorized use of the Platform as contemplated by this Agreement does not and will not infringe, misappropriate, or otherwise violate any Intellectual Property Rights of any third party;
185: 185	(e) the Platform and all services provided hereunder will comply with all applicable laws, including GLBA and CCPA/CPRA;
186: 186	(f) Vendor will maintain all insurance coverages required by Article 12 during the Term and for two (2) years thereafter; and
187: 187	(g) no open-source software included in the Platform is licensed under terms that would require Customer to disclose or distribute its proprietary software or Customer Data (e.g., no copyleft obligations that flow through to Customer's use).
188: 188	Customer's sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor's sole and exclusive liability, for any breach of the warranty set forth in Section 8.2(a) shall be for Vendor, at its option, to (i) repair or replace the non-conforming Platform functionality so that it conforms to the Documentation, or (ii) if Vendor is unable to repair or replace such functionality within a commercially reasonable period, terminate this Agreement and refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Fees attributable to the period following such termination.
189: 189	Section 8.3 — Disclaimer
190: 190	EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 8, VENDOR MAKES NO WARRANTIES OF ANY KIND, WHETHER EXPRESS, IMPLIED, STATUTORY, OR OTHERWISE, WITH RESPECT TO THE PLATFORM, THE IMPLEMENTATION SERVICES, THE BASE MODEL, ANY DERIVATIVE MODELS, OR ANY OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION ANY WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, NON-INFRINGEMENT, TITLE, ACCURACY, COMPLETENESS, RELIABILITY, OR QUALITY OF OUTPUTS. VENDOR DOES NOT WARRANT THAT THE PLATFORM WILL BE ERROR-FREE, UNINTERRUPTED, OR FREE OF HARMFUL COMPONENTS, OR THAT THE OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM WILL BE ACCURATE, COMPLETE, OR SUITABLE FOR ANY PARTICULAR PURPOSE. CUSTOMER ACKNOWLEDGES THAT LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS ARE PROBABILISTIC IN NATURE AND THAT OUTPUTS MAY CONTAIN ERRORS, HALLUCINATIONS, OR INACCURACIES, AND CUSTOMER IS SOLELY RESPONSIBLE FOR EVALUATING AND VALIDATING ALL OUTPUTS FOR ITS INTENDED USE.
191: 191	ARTICLE 9 — SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDITS
192: 192	Section 9.1 — Uptime
193: 193	Vendor shall  maintain Platform availability of at least  ninety-nine and ninety-five hundredths percent (99.95%) in any calendar month (the "Uptime SLA"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:
194: 194	Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100
195: 195	For purposes of the Uptime SLA, "Downtime" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor's monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in  this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer's systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer's acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer's access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).
196: 196	Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month, shall require at least seventy-two (72) hours' advance written notice to Customer's designated technical contact, and shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable. Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
197: 197	Section 9.2 — Latency
198: 198	Vendor shall  maintain API response latency at or below  four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤  400 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor's internal monitoring systems at the Platform's API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor's receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor's transmission of the corresponding API response.
199: 199	Section 9.3 — Model Accuracy
200: 200	Vendor shall  maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above  zero point ninety-four (F1 ≥ 0.94), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset  established during the implementation process, following the conclusion of the Stabilization Period. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer's production document processing workloads.
201: 201	During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.90, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.
202: 202	Section 9.4 — Service Credits
203: 203	In the event Vendor fails to meet the  Uptime SLA, API Latency target, or Model Accuracy target in any  applicable measurement period, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a "Service Credit"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the  SLA failure occurred.

19	ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS

20	As used in this Agreement, the following capitalized terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used in this Agreement that are not defined in this Article 1 shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

21	"Affiliate" means, with respect to any Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with such Party. 57	ARTICLE 2 — LICENSE GRANT AND SCOPE OF USE
58	Section 2.1 — License Grant

59	Subject to and conditioned upon Customer's compliance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including timely payment of all Fees, Vendor hereby grants to Customer a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable(except as permitted under Section 14.4), non-sublicensable (except to Affiliates) license during the Term to access and use the Platform solely for Customer's internal business operations in connection with Customer's lending technology product known as LendStream. The license granted hereunder includes the right to access and use the Platform through the APIs provided by Vendor, to submit Customer Data for processing through the Platform, and to receive and use the outputs generated by the Platform in connection with LendStream. This license is further conditioned on Customer's compliance with the Documentation and all applicable laws, rules, and regulations.
60	Section 2.2 — Scope of Authorized Use

61	Customer may permit its employees, and authorized contractors who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in Article 7, to access and use the Platform on Customer's behalf and in furtherance of Customer's authorized use hereunder. Customer shall be responsible for all acts and omissions of its employees and authorized contractors in connection with their access to and use of the Platform. Use of the Platform is limited to the processing, analysis, and classification of Customer Data in support of LendStream's document processing workflows. Customer shall not use the Platform for any purpose other than as expressly authorized by this Agreement. Customer shall not exceed the Included API Calls in any Contract Year, except as subject to the overage charges set forth in Section 4.3.
62	Section 2.3 — Restrictions
63	Customer acknowledges that the Platform and Base Model represent proprietary technology of Vendor. Customer shall not, and shall not permit any third party to:

64	(a) reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, or otherwise attempt to derive the source code, algorithms, data structures, or underlying ideas of the Platform or the Base Model, except to the extent that such restriction is expressly prohibited by applicable law notwithstanding a contractual prohibition;

65	(b) sublicense, sell, resell, lease, rent, loan, distribute, or otherwise make available the Platform or any component thereof to any third party, whether as a service bureau, managed service, or otherwise;

66	(c) use the Platform or any output thereof for competitive benchmarking, competitive analysis, or to develop, train, or improve a product or service that competes with the Platform or any of Vendor's other products or services;
67	(d) remove, obscure, alter, or deface any proprietary notices, labels, or marks on or in the Platform, the Documentation, or any output thereof;

68	(e) access the Platform other than through the APIs and access mechanisms provided by Vendor, including without limitation by scraping, crawling, or using any automated means not expressly authorized by Vendor;

69	(f) attempt to extract, reconstruct, distill, or reverse engineer model weights, architectures, training data, or any other proprietary components from the Platform, whether through prompt injection, model inversion, membership inference, or any other technique; or

70	(g) use the Platform in any manner that violates applicable law or regulation, or that infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates the Intellectual Property Rights or other rights of any third party.
71	Section 2.4 — Reservation of Rights

72	Except for the limited license expressly granted in Section 2.1, Vendor reserves all rights in and to the Platformand the Base Model (excluding Customer-Trained Adaptations), including all Intellectual Property Rights therein. No implied licenses are granted under this Agreement by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Customer's right to access and use the Platform is limited to the express license grant set forth in Section 2.1, and all other rights are expressly reserved by Vendor. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to grant Customer any right to access the source code or model weights of the Platform or the Base Model.
73	ARTICLE 3 — IMPLEMENTATION AND TRAINING SERVICES
74	Section 3.1 — Implementation Services

75	Vendor shall perform the Implementation Services as described in the initial Statement of Work attached hereto as Exhibit A (the "Initial SOW") and any additional Statements of Work that may be executed by the Parties from time to time pursuant to this Article 3. The Implementation Services under the Initial SOW shall include, without limitation: (a) provisioning and configuration of Customer's dedicated Platform environment; (b) API integration of the Platform with Customer's LendStream product; (c) fine-tuning of the Base Model using Customer Data to optimize the Platform's performance for Customer's specific document processing requirements; (d) initial accuracy validation and testing of the fine-tuned model; and (e) initial training of Customer's designated personnel on the use and operation of the Platform. All Implementation Services shall be performed by Vendor personnel who are qualified and experienced in the relevant subject matter.
76	Section 3.2 — Implementation Milestones
77	The Implementation Services shall be performed in accordance with the following milestones, as further described in Exhibit A:

78	Milestone 1 — SOW Execution. Execution of the Initial SOW by both Parties. Achievement of Milestone 1 shall trigger payment of the first installment of the Implementation Fee as set forth in Section 4.2(a).

79	Milestone 2 — Go-Live. Successful achievement of Go-Live, targeted for October 1, 2025, at which point the Platform shall be made available for production use by Customer. Achievement of Milestone 2 shall trigger payment of the second installment of the Implementation Fee as set forth in Section 4.2(b). Go-Live shall be conditioned upon the Platform performing materially in accordance with the Documentation, as mutually confirmed by the Parties through the acceptance process described in  Exhibit A and Section 3.5.

80	Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve the targeted Go-Live date, but the targeted Go-Live date is an estimate only and shall not constitute a guaranteed delivery date. Delays caused by Customer's failure to fulfill its cooperation obligations under Section 3.3 shall extend the targeted Go-Live date by a commensurate period.
81	Section 3.3 — Customer Cooperation

82	Customer acknowledges that Vendor's ability to perform the Implementation Services is dependent upon Customer's timely cooperation and assistance. Customer shall provide reasonable cooperation in connection with the Implementation Services, including without limitation: (a) timely provision of Customer Data in the format and quality reasonably specified by Vendor; (b) access to Customer's systems and environments as reasonably necessary for Vendor to perform API integration and testing; (c) designation of qualified Customer personnel with appropriate subject matter expertise to serve as points of contact and to participate in the implementation process, including providing timely feedback and approvals; and (d) such other cooperation as may be reasonably requested by Vendor and described in the applicable Statement of Work. Customer's failure to provide timely cooperation may result in delays in the Implementation Services, and Vendor shall not be responsible for any such delays to the extent caused by Customer's failure to perform its cooperation obligations under this Section 3.3.
83	Section 3.4 — Change Orders

84	Any changes to the scope, timeline, deliverables, or fees for Implementation Services shall be documented in a mutually agreed written change order signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. No change to the Implementation Services shall be binding unless set forth in a duly executed change order. Each change order shall specify the nature of the change, any impact on the project timeline and milestones, and any additional fees associated with the change. Vendor shall not be obligated to perform any work outside the scope of an executed Statement of Work or change order.
85	[ADDED: ### Section 3.5 — Acceptance Testing

86	Following completion of implementation and prior to Go-Live, Vendor shall conduct acceptance testing in accordance with mutually agreed test plans and acceptance criteria set forth in the applicable Statement of Work. Customer shall have fifteen (15) business days to review acceptance test results and either accept or reject the deliverables with written specification of deficiencies. Vendor shall correct all material deficiencies and resubmit for acceptance within ten (10) business days. If Vendor fails to correct all material deficiencies after two (2) remediation cycles, Customer may escalate the matter pursuant to the dispute resolution procedures in Section 14.2 of this Agreement.]
87	ARTICLE 4 — FEES AND PAYMENT
88	Section 4.1 — Annual Platform Fee

89	In consideration of the license and access rights granted hereunder, Customer shall pay to Vendor an annual platform fee of Two Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars ($2,400,000) per Contract Year (the "Annual Platform Fee"). The Annual Platform Fee shall be invoiced by Vendor in equal monthly installments of Two Hundred Thousand Dollars ($200,000) per month, with each monthly invoice due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice. Vendor shall issue monthly invoices on or about the first business day of each calendar month during the Term, beginning with the first calendar month following the Effective Date.
90	Section 4.2 — Implementation Fee

91	In consideration of the Implementation Services described in Article 3 and Exhibit A, Customer shall pay to Vendor a one-time implementation and fine-tuning fee of Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($850,000) (the "Implementation Fee"). The Implementation Fee shall be payable in two (2) equal installments of Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars ($425,000) each, as follows:
92	(a) First Installment. Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars ($425,000), due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice following execution of the Initial SOW (Milestone 1).
93	(b) Second Installment. Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars ($425,000), due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice following achievement of Go-Live (Milestone 2).
94	Section 4.3 — Overage Fees

95	The Annual Platform Fee includes forty million (40,000,000) API calls per Contract Year (the "Included API Calls"). API calls made by Customer in excess of the Included API Calls during any Contract Year shall be invoiced by Vendor at a rate of twelve-thousandths of a dollar ($0.012) per API call (the "Overage Rate"). Overage Fees shall be invoiced monthly in arrears, based on Vendor's metering and usage data for the applicable calendar month. Each such invoice shall include a summary of API call usage for the month, including the number of API calls consumed and the number of remaining Included API Calls for the applicable Contract Year. Overage Fee invoices shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice.
96	Section 4.4 — Taxes

97	All Fees set forth in this Agreement are exclusive of any and all applicable taxes, duties, levies, or similar governmental charges (collectively, "Taxes"). Customer shall be responsible for, and shall pay, all sales, use, value-added, goods and services, withholding, and similar Taxes imposed on or in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, excluding taxes based on Vendor's net income, capital, or franchise taxes assessed against Vendor. If Vendor is required by law to collect any Taxes from Customer, Vendor shall include such Taxes on the applicable invoice and Customer shall remit payment of such Taxes together with the applicable Fees. If Customer is required to withhold any Taxes from amounts payable to Vendor, Customer shall gross up the payment so that Vendor receives the full amount of the invoiced Fees after deduction of such withholding Taxes.
98	Section 4.5 — Late Payments

99	Any undisputed Fees not paid when due shall accrue interest at the lesser of (a) one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (18% per annum) or (b) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, from the date such payment was due until the date such payment is received in full by Vendor. In addition, Vendor may, upon at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice to Customer, suspend Customer's access to the Platform if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid for more than forty-five (45) days past its due date, and such suspension shall continue until all outstanding amounts, including accrued interest, have been paid in full. The foregoing remedies are in addition to, and not in lieu of, any other remedies available to Vendor under this Agreement or applicable law.
100	Section 4.6 — Total Contract Value
101	For informational purposes and clarity, the total contract value for the Initial Term (exclusive of Overage Fees and Taxes) is as follows:
102	(a) Annual Platform Fees for three (3) Contract Years: $2,400,000 × 3 = $7,200,000;
103	(b) Implementation Fee (one-time): $850,000;

105	The foregoing total contract value is an estimate for informational purposes only and does not include any Overage Fees, Taxes, or fees for additional Statements of Work that may be executed during the Term. The total contract value does not limit Vendor's right to invoice for Overage Fees or other amounts payable under this Agreement.
106	[ADDED: ### Section 4.7 — Right of Set-Off

107	Customer shall have the right to set off any amounts owed to Customer under this Agreement (including Service Credits under Article 9 and indemnification obligations under Article 11) against amounts payable by Customer to Vendor.]
108	[ADDED: ### Section 4.8 — Audit Rights

109	Vendor shall maintain accurate books and records relating to overage calculations and API call volumes. Customer shall have the right, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice, no more than once per Contract Year, to audit or have an independent third-party auditor audit Vendor's relevant records to verify the accuracy of invoiced overages. If an audit reveals an overcharge exceeding five percent (5%) of the audited amount, Vendor shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit and promptly refund the overcharge.]
110	ARTICLE 5 — INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
111	Section 5.1 — Vendor IP Ownership

112	As between the Parties, Vendor is and shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to: (a) the Platform (excluding Customer-Trained Adaptations); (b) the Base Model; (c)  all Derivative Models (excluding Customer-Trained Adaptations); and  (d) all improvements, enhancements, updates, upgrades, modifications, and derivative works of any of the foregoing (excluding Customer-Trained Adaptations), together with all Intellectual Property Rights therein and thereto, regardless of whether such items are created by Vendor independently, in collaboration with Customer, or through the processing of Customer Data.

114	As between the Parties, Customer is and shall  the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to all  [ADDED: Customer-Trained Adaptations, including all fine-tuned weights, adapter layers, LoRA matrices, and any other model parameters generated through fine-tuning of the Base Model using Customer Data, together with all Intellectual Property Rights therein. Vendor hereby assigns and agrees to assign to Customer all right, title, and interest in and to such Customer-Trained Adaptations, effective upon creation. Vendor shall execute all documents and take all actions reasonably requested by Customer to evidence or perfect Customer's ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations.

115	Vendor is granted a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Customer-Trained Adaptations solely to the extent necessary to provide the Platform and perform its obligations under this Agreement during the Term. Such license shall automatically terminate upon expiration or termination of this Agreement.]
116	[ADDED: ### Section 5.3 — Customer Data Ownership

117	As between the Parties, Customer is and shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to all Customer Data, including all Intellectual Property Rights therein. Vendor's right to access, use, and process Customer Data is strictly limited to providing the Platform and performing its obligations under this Agreement as a service provider, and for no other purpose.
