119	If Customer or any of its employees, contractors, or agents provides any suggestions, enhancement requests, ideas, recommendations, corrections, or other feedback regarding the Platform, the Documentation, or any of Vendor's products or services (collectively, "Feedback"), Customer hereby grants to Vendor a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid-up, transferable, sublicensable license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, create derivative works from, distribute, display, perform, and otherwise exploit such Feedback in any manner and for any purpose, without restriction, attribution, or compensation to Customer. Customer acknowledges that Vendor may use Feedback to improve the Platform, develop new features, or create new products or services, and that Vendor shall have no obligation to implement or incorporate any Feedback.
120	Section 5.[DELETED: 4] [ADDED: 5] — No Other Rights

121	Except as expressly set forth in this Article 5 and the license granted in Section 2.1, neither Party grants the other Party any right, title, or interest in or to its Intellectual Property Rights, whether by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to grant Customer any rights in Vendor's trade secrets, proprietary algorithms, model architectures, training methodologies, or other confidential technical information, except as expressly provided herein.
122	[ADDED: ## ARTICLE 5A — TECHNOLOGY ESCROW
123	Section 5A.1 — Escrow Arrangement

124	Within thirty (30) days of the Effective Date, Vendor shall enter into a three-party escrow agreement with Customer and Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. (the "Escrow Agent"), in a form reasonably satisfactory to Customer, pursuant to which Vendor shall deposit the Escrow Materials.
125	Section 5A.2 — Escrow Deposits
126	Vendor shall deposit and maintain current versions of the following Escrow Materials:
127	(a) Complete source code for the Base Model, including all build scripts, compilers, and tools necessary to compile and deploy the Base Model;
128	(b) All Customer-Trained Adaptations, including fine-tuned adapter weights, training configuration files, and pipeline artifacts;
129	(c) All Documentation necessary to build, deploy, and operate the Platform;
130	(d) Complete dependency list, third-party library inventory, and license information.
131	Vendor shall update the Escrow Materials within thirty (30) days following any material update to the deposited materials, and in any event no less frequently than quarterly.
132	Section 5A.3 — Release Conditions
133	The Escrow Agent shall release the Escrow Materials to Customer upon the occurrence of any of the following release conditions:

134	(a) Vendor becomes the subject of a voluntary or involuntary petition in bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership, liquidation, or similar proceeding, or makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors;
135	(b) Vendor commits a material breach of this Agreement that remains uncured for more than sixty (60) days after Customer's written notice specifying the breach;
136	(c) Vendor ceases to support, maintain, or make available the Platform commercially, or publicly announces its intention to do so.

137	Upon release, Customer shall receive a non-exclusive, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide license to use, modify, compile, and deploy the Escrow Materials solely for Customer's internal business purposes in connection with LendStream.
138	Section 5A.4 — Escrow Costs
139	Vendor shall bear all costs associated with establishing and maintaining the escrow arrangement, including Escrow Agent fees and deposit verification costs.
140	Section 5A.5 — Verification

141	Customer shall have the right, no more than once per Contract Year, to request verification by the Escrow Agent or a mutually agreed third-party technical expert that the Escrow Materials are complete, current, and sufficient to build and deploy the Platform. Vendor shall cooperate with such verification. The cost of verification shall be borne by Customer, unless verification reveals a material deficiency, in which case Vendor shall bear the cost.]
142	ARTICLE 6 — DATA PROCESSING AND PRIVACY
143	Section 6.1 — Customer Data Processing

144	Vendor shall process Customer Data solely for the  purpose of providing the Platform and performing Vendor's obligations under this Agreement. Vendor shall not  process Customer Data  for any  other  purpose, including without limitation training, improving, or benchmarking the Base Model or any Derivative Models for the benefit of Vendor or any third party. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data to any third party.
145	Section 6.2 — [DELETED: Controller] [ADDED: Service Provider / Processor] Status

146	 Vendor shall process Customer Data solely as a service provider (as defined in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag)) and processor on behalf of Customer. Vendor shall not be deemed an independent controller with respect to any processing of Customer Data. Vendor shall certify its status as a service provider under the CCPA/CPRA in the Data Processing Addendum (Exhibit D).
147	Section 6.3 — Compliance with Laws

148	Each Party shall comply with all applicable data protection and privacy laws, rules, and regulations in connection with its processing of Customer Data under this Agreement, including without limitation: (a) the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 6801–6809, and its implementing regulations, including Regulation S-P (17 C.F.R. Part 248) and the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314) ("GLBA"), to the extent applicable to the processing of NPPI; (b) the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act of 2020, Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1798.100–1798.199.100 ("CCPA/CPRA"), to the extent applicable; and (c) any other applicable federal, state, or international data protection or privacy laws.  Vendor's obligations as a service provider under CCPA/CPRA are further set forth in the Data Processing Addendum (Exhibit D).
149	Section 6.4 — Security Measures

150	Vendor shall implement and maintain throughout the Term  administrative, technical, and physical safeguards that are no less protective than industry-standard measures, including SOC 2 Type II controls, designed to protect Customer Data against unauthorized access, acquisition, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Vendor's security program shall include: (a) encryption of Customer Data in transit (using TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (using AES-256 or equivalent); (b) access controls, including multi-factor authentication, role-based access, and least-privilege principles; (c) regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing; (d) intrusion detection and prevention systems; (e) security incident response procedures; and (f) employee security awareness training. Vendor shall, upon Customer's reasonable request and no more than once per twelve (12)-month period, provide Customer with a summary of Vendor's then-current security measures and any SOC 2 Type II or equivalent audit reports covering Vendor's information security controls.
151	Section 6.5 — Data Breach Notification

152	In the event of any confirmed or reasonably suspected security breach involving the unauthorized access, acquisition, use, or disclosure of Customer Data (a "Security Breach"), Vendor shall: (a) notify Customer of the Security Breach  within seventy-two (72) hours of  discovery of the Security Breach; (b) promptly investigate the Security Breach and take reasonable steps to contain, mitigate, and remediate the Security Breach; (c) provide Customer with reasonably detailed information regarding the nature and scope of the Security Breach, including the categories and approximate number of  data subjects affected, the  measures taken or proposed to address  the Security Breach, and the identity and contact information of Vendor's data protection officer or other contact point; and (d) cooperate with Customer in Customer's investigation, response, and notification obligations in connection with the Security Breach. The obligations set forth in this Section 6.5 shall not be construed as an acknowledgment by Vendor of any fault or liability with respect to the Security Breach.
153	[ADDED: ### Section 6.6 — Sub-Processors

154	Vendor shall not engage any sub-processor to process Customer Data without Customer's prior written consent. Vendor shall maintain a list of sub-processors and provide such list to Customer upon request. Vendor shall impose data protection obligations on sub-processors that are no less protective than those set forth in this Agreement and the DPA. Vendor shall remain fully liable for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors.]
155	Section 6.[DELETED: 6] [ADDED: 7] — Return and Deletion of Data

156	Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, Vendor shall, at Customer's written election made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration, either (a) return Customer Data to Customer in a commercially reasonable format designated by Customer, or (b) securely delete or destroy all Customer Data in Vendor's possession or control, including all copies, backups, and archives thereof. Vendor shall complete such return or deletion within  thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of Customer's written request. Upon completion of the return or deletion, Vendor shall certify in writing to Customer that all Customer Data has been returned or deleted in accordance with this Section 6. 7.  Vendor shall not retain any Customer Data in any form following termination, except as required by applicable law, in which case Vendor shall (i) isolate such data, (ii) continue to protect it in accordance with this Agreement, and (iii) delete it as soon as the retention obligation expires. For the avoidance of doubt, no exception shall apply for de-identified or aggregated data, which shall also be returned or deleted upon Customer's request.
157	[ADDED: ### Section 6.8 — Data Processing Addendum

158	The Parties shall execute the Data Processing Addendum attached as Exhibit D contemporaneously with this Agreement. The DPA is incorporated into and forms part of this Agreement. In the event of any conflict between the DPA and this Agreement, the DPA shall control with respect to data protection matters.]
159	ARTICLE 7 — CONFIDENTIALITY
160	Section 7.1 — Definition of Confidential Information

161	"Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the "Disclosing Party") to the other Party (the "Receiving Party") in connection with this Agreement, whether disclosed orally, in writing, electronically, or by any other means, and whether or not marked or designated as "confidential," "proprietary," or with any similar legend, that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Confidential Information includes: (a) business plans, strategies, forecasts, and financial information; (b) technical information, including source code, algorithms, model architectures, model weights, training data, APIs, and system designs; (c) trade secrets; (d) customer lists, supplier lists, and pricing information; (e) product roadmaps and development plans; and (f) the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including all pricing, fee, and commercial terms. Customer Data shall be deemed Confidential Information of Customer regardless of whether it is marked or designated as confidential.

162	Confidential Information shall not include information that: (i) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of or breach by the Receiving Party; (ii) was already known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by the Receiving Party's written records; (iii) is rightfully received by the Receiving Party from a third party without restriction on disclosure and without breach of any obligation of confidentiality owed to the Disclosing Party; or (iv) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, as evidenced by the Receiving Party's written records.
163	Section 7.2 — Obligations

164	The Receiving Party shall: (a) hold the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in strict confidence; (b) not disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to any third party except as expressly permitted under Section 7.3; (c) use the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information solely for the purposes of performing its obligations or exercising its rights under this Agreement; and (d) protect the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information using  measures that are  no less protective than those used by the Receiving Party to protect its own most sensitive confidential information, but in no event less than a reasonable standard of care.

165	The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article 7 shall remain in effect during the Term and for a period of five (5) years following the  date of disclosure; provided, however, that the confidentiality obligations with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law shall continue for so long as such information remains a trade secret.
166	Section 7.3 — Permitted Disclosures

167	The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to its employees, officers, directors, agents, contractors, consultants, advisors, and Affiliates who have a legitimate need to know such information for the purposes of this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article 7 (collectively, "Authorized Recipients"). The Receiving Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Article 7 by its Authorized Recipients.

168	The Receiving Party may also disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, court order, subpoena, or other legal process, provided that the Receiving Party: (a) provides the Disclosing Party with prompt written notice of such requirement (to the extent legally permitted) so that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy; (b) cooperates with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party's expense, in seeking such protective order or other remedy; and (c) discloses only the minimum amount of Confidential Information necessary to comply with such requirement. Any Confidential Information disclosed pursuant to a legal compulsion shall retain its confidential status for all other purposes under this Agreement.
169	[ADDED: ### Section 7.4 — Injunctive Relief

170	Each Party acknowledges that a breach of this Article 7 may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be an inadequate remedy. Accordingly, each Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive or other equitable relief from any court of competent jurisdiction without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting a bond or other security.]
171	ARTICLE 8 — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
172	Section 8.1 — Mutual Representations and Warranties
173	Each Party hereby represents and warrants to the other Party as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Effective Date that:
174	(a) it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its formation;
175	(b) it has full corporate or limited liability company power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to perform its obligations hereunder;
176	(c) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate or limited liability company action;

177	(d) this Agreement constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors' rights generally and to general principles of equity; and

178	(e) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement will not (i) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of any provision of such Party's organizational documents, (ii) violate any applicable law, rule, or regulation, or (iii) conflict with, result in a breach of, or constitute a default under any material agreement or instrument to which such Party is a party or by which it is bound.
179	Section 8.2 — Vendor Representations and Warranties
180	Vendor hereby represents and warrants to Customer that:

181	(a) the Platform, when used in accordance with the Documentation and this Agreement, will perform materially in accordance with the functional specifications set forth in the Documentation during the Term;

182	(b) the Implementation Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, consistent with generally accepted industry standards for similar services, using personnel with the requisite skill, experience, and qualifications;

183	(c) Vendor has all rights necessary to grant the license set forth in Section 2.1, free and clear of any liens, encumbrances, or restrictions that would materially impair Customer's exercise of the rights granted thereunder;

184	(d)  Customer's authorized use of the Platform as contemplated by this Agreement does not and will not infringe, misappropriate, or otherwise violate any Intellectual Property Rights of any third party;
185	(e) the Platform and all services provided hereunder will comply with all applicable laws, including GLBA and CCPA/CPRA;
186	(f) Vendor will maintain all insurance coverages required by Article 12 during the Term and for two (2) years thereafter; and

187	(g) no open-source software included in the Platform is licensed under terms that would require Customer to disclose or distribute its proprietary software or Customer Data (e.g., no copyleft obligations that flow through to Customer's use).

188	Customer's sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor's sole and exclusive liability, for any breach of the warranty set forth in Section 8.2(a) shall be for Vendor, at its option, to (i) repair or replace the non-conforming Platform functionality so that it conforms to the Documentation, or (ii) if Vendor is unable to repair or replace such functionality within a commercially reasonable period, terminate this Agreement and refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Fees attributable to the period following such termination.
189	Section 8.3 — Disclaimer

190	EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 8, VENDOR MAKES NO WARRANTIES OF ANY KIND, WHETHER EXPRESS, IMPLIED, STATUTORY, OR OTHERWISE, WITH RESPECT TO THE PLATFORM, THE IMPLEMENTATION SERVICES, THE BASE MODEL, ANY DERIVATIVE MODELS, OR ANY OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION ANY WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, NON-INFRINGEMENT, TITLE, ACCURACY, COMPLETENESS, RELIABILITY, OR QUALITY OF OUTPUTS. VENDOR DOES NOT WARRANT THAT THE PLATFORM WILL BE ERROR-FREE, UNINTERRUPTED, OR FREE OF HARMFUL COMPONENTS, OR THAT THE OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM WILL BE ACCURATE, COMPLETE, OR SUITABLE FOR ANY PARTICULAR PURPOSE. CUSTOMER ACKNOWLEDGES THAT LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS ARE PROBABILISTIC IN NATURE AND THAT OUTPUTS MAY CONTAIN ERRORS, HALLUCINATIONS, OR INACCURACIES, AND CUSTOMER IS SOLELY RESPONSIBLE FOR EVALUATING AND VALIDATING ALL OUTPUTS FOR ITS INTENDED USE.
191	ARTICLE 9 — SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDITS
192	Section 9.1 — Uptime

193	Vendor shall  maintain Platform availability of at least  ninety-nine and ninety-five hundredths percent (99.95%) in any calendar month (the "Uptime SLA"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:
194	Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100

195	For purposes of the Uptime SLA, "Downtime" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor's monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in  this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer's systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer's acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer's access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).

196	Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month, shall require at least seventy-two (72) hours' advance written notice to Customer's designated technical contact, and shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable. Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
197	Section 9.2 — Latency

198	Vendor shall  maintain API response latency at or below  four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤  400 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor's internal monitoring systems at the Platform's API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor's receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor's transmission of the corresponding API response.
199	Section 9.3 — Model Accuracy

200	Vendor shall  maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above  zero point ninety-four (F1 ≥ 0.94), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset  established during the implementation process, following the conclusion of the Stabilization Period. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer's production document processing workloads.

201	During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.90, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.
202	Section 9.4 — Service Credits

203	In the event Vendor fails to meet the  Uptime SLA, API Latency target, or Model Accuracy target in any  applicable measurement period, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a "Service Credit"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the  SLA failure occurred.

def shade(cell, fill):
    tcPr=cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr(); shd=tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None: shd=OxmlElement('w:shd'); tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'),fill)

def set_cell_text(cell,text,bold=False,size=8.2,color=None):
    cell.text=''
    p=cell.paragraphs[0]; p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0)
    r=p.add_run(text); r.bold=bold; r.font.size=Pt(size)
    if color: r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(color)
    cell.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.TOP
